title: Entanglement Structure And Matrix Inequalities From Isotypic Measurements
authors: Albert Rico, Dmitry Grinko, Robin Krebs, And Lin Htoo Zaw
abstract:
Author(s): Albert Rico, Dmitry Grinko, Robin Krebs, and Lin Htoo Zaw

We detect entanglement partitions of multipartite quantum systems by exploiting their inherent symmetries. Structures like genuinely multipartite entanglement, [MATH]-separability, and entanglement depth are detected as very special cases. This formulation enables us to characterize all entanglement pa…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 100203] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a symmetry-based framework using isotypic measurements to systematically detect entanglement partitions in multipartite quantum systems.
motivation: Detecting and characterizing multipartite entanglement is a fundamental challenge, and existing criteria are often ad hoc or limited to specific cases.
method: The authors exploit inherent symmetries of multipartite systems and derive matrix inequalities from isotypic measurements to characterize entanglement partitions.
result: The framework unifies detection of genuinely multipartite entanglement, k-separability, and entanglement depth as special cases.
conclusion: This provides a general and systematic tool for entanglement detection, with implications for quantum information processing and foundational studies.

title: Experimental Observation Of Multimode Quantum Phase Transitions In A Superconducting Bose-Hubbard Simulator
authors: Claudia Castillo-Moreno, Théo Sépulcre, Timo Hillmann, Kazi Rafsanjani Amin, Mikael Kervinen, And Simone Gasparinetti
abstract:
Author(s): Claudia Castillo-Moreno, Théo Sépulcre, Timo Hillmann, Kazi Rafsanjani Amin, Mikael Kervinen, and Simone Gasparinetti

By harnessing cross-Kerr interactions in a superconducting microwave Bose-Hubbard lattice, an experimental study reveals a first-order multimode dissipative phase transition in one dimension.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033030] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of a first-order multimode dissipative phase transition in a superconducting Bose-Hubbard simulator.
motivation: To investigate multimode quantum phase transitions and non-equilibrium many-body phenomena in a controlled quantum simulator.
method: Utilized a superconducting microwave Bose-Hubbard lattice with cross-Kerr interactions to implement the model and probe the phase transition.
result: Demonstrated a first-order multimode dissipative phase transition in one dimension, showcasing the simulator's capability to access non-equilibrium physics.
conclusion: The experiment establishes superconducting circuits as a powerful platform for studying quantum phase transitions and opens avenues for exploring complex many-body dynamics.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A minimal quantum-particle-detector model reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, assessing the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: To understand the fundamental thermodynamic cost of information acquisition in quantum detection, and how measurement accuracy relates to entropy production.
method: They present a minimal model of a quantum-particle detector as an autonomous machine, analyzing its nonequilibrium thermodynamics.
result: They demonstrate fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the cost of information gain.
conclusion: The study offers insights into the thermodynamic constraints on information acquisition in quantum systems.

title: Room-Temperature Storage Of Entanglement In A Silicon Carbide Quantum Node
authors: Shuo Ren, Rui-Jian Liang, Qi-Cheng Hu, Zhen-Xuan He, Ji-Yang Zhou, Wu-Xi Lin, Zhi-He Hao, Tao Tu, Jin-Shi Xu, Chuan-Feng Li, And Guang-Can Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Shuo Ren, Rui-Jian Liang, Qi-Cheng Hu, Zhen-Xuan He, Ji-Yang Zhou, Wu-Xi Lin, Zhi-He Hao, Tao Tu, Jin-Shi Xu, Chuan-Feng Li, and Guang-Can Guo

Robust entanglement at room temperature is a central challenge for solid-state quantum information processing and quantum-enhanced sensing. Here we demonstrate room-temperature storage of entanglement in a silicon carbide (SiC) quantum node by coherently transferring an electron-nuclear entangled st…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 100803] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates room-temperature storage of entanglement in a silicon carbide quantum node, a key capability for quantum networks.
motivation: Robust entanglement at room temperature is challenging but essential for practical solid-state quantum information processing and quantum-enhanced sensing.
method: The authors coherently transfer an electron-nuclear entangled state to nuclear spins in a silicon carbide defect for storage at room temperature.
result: They successfully store and later retrieve entanglement at room temperature, showing the viability of SiC as a quantum memory platform.
conclusion: This work advances quantum memory technology, enabling future quantum network nodes that can operate at ambient conditions.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that a cos(φ) coupling suppresses measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout, leading to higher readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions during dispersive readout limit readout fidelity and cause leakage, motivating the need for improved coupling schemes.
method: The authors implement a cos(φ) coupler between the transmon and resonator and perform numerical simulations to analyze the readout dynamics.
result: The cos(φ) coupling significantly reduces measurement-induced transitions and improves readout fidelity compared to standard transverse coupling.
conclusion: This coupling approach offers a practical way to enhance transmon readout, benefiting scalable quantum computing.

title: Waiting-time-based Entropy Estimators In Continuous Space Without Markovian Events
authors: Jonas H. Fritz And Udo Seifert
abstract:
Author(s): Jonas H. Fritz and Udo Seifert

Estimating entropy production in continuous systems that can only be observed with a limited resolution remains an open problem in stochastic thermodynamics. Existing estimators based on the measurement of waiting-time distributions either require the detection of Markovian events, which uniquely de…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034109] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops entropy estimators based on waiting-time distributions that work in continuous systems even when events are not Markovian, extending the applicability of such approaches.
motivation: Estimating entropy production in continuous systems with limited resolution is challenging; existing waiting-time estimators require detection of Markovian events, which is often not feasible.
method: The authors propose new estimators that utilize waiting-time distributions without relying on Markovian event detection, using a coarse-grained description of continuous trajectories.
result: The estimators are validated on model systems and shown to accurately estimate entropy production even when events are non-Markovian.
conclusion: This work broadens the methods for entropy estimation in stochastic thermodynamics, making them more practical for realistic experimental scenarios.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy to certify that quantum measurements cannot be simulated by projective ones, with an experimental proof on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying the nature of measurements is fundamental for quantum information tasks, especially in device-independent scenarios, and previous methods were incomplete or lacked experimental validation.
method: The authors develop a complete SDP hierarchy for bounding the projective simulability of quantum measurements and implement the certification protocol on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
result: The hierarchy provides robust certification criteria, and the experiment successfully demonstrates the impossibility of simulating the implemented non-projective measurements by projective ones.
conclusion: The work advances measurement certification theory and offers a practical tool for quantum device characterization with implications for quantum foundations and information.

title: Passive Quantum State Transfer In A Dispersion-Engineered Waveguide
authors: Zeyu Kuang, Oliver Diekmann, Lorenz Fischer, Stefan Rotter, And Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero
abstract:
Author(s): Zeyu Kuang, Oliver Diekmann, Lorenz Fischer, Stefan Rotter, and Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero

High-fidelity state transfer between two qubits is fundamentally limited by time-reversal symmetry: one qubit emits a photon with a certain temporal pulse shape, whereas a second qubit requires the time-reversed pulse shape to efficiently absorb this photon. This limitation is often overcome by intr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 103605] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a passive method for high-fidelity quantum state transfer between qubits using a dispersion-engineered waveguide to circumvent time-reversal symmetry limitations.
motivation: State transfer between qubits is limited by time-reversal symmetry, requiring time-reversed photon pulse shapes for efficient absorption, which typically demands active control. A passive approach could simplify implementations.
method: The authors engineer the waveguide dispersion to shape the emitted photon and match the absorption profile of the receiving qubit without active pulse shaping or temporal control.
result: They achieve high-fidelity passive quantum state transfer, overcoming the time-reversal constraint and enabling efficient qubit-to-qubit communication.
conclusion: The dispersion-engineered waveguide provides a scalable and simplified route for quantum state transfer, potentially advancing quantum network architectures.

title: Analytically Continuing The Randomized Measurement Toolbox
authors: Akash Vijay, Ayush Raj, Jonah Kudler-Flam, Benoît Vermersch, Andreas Elben, And Laimei Nie
abstract:
Author(s): Akash Vijay, Ayush Raj, Jonah Kudler-Flam, Benoît Vermersch, Andreas Elben, and Laimei Nie

We develop a framework for extracting nonpolynomial analytic functions of density matrices in randomized measurement experiments by a method of analytical continuation. A central advantage of this approach, dubbed stabilized analytic continuation (SAC), is its robustness to statistical noise arising…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 100202] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: Introduces 'stabilized analytic continuation' to extract nonpolynomial analytic functions of density matrices from randomized measurements, enhancing noise robustness.
motivation: Randomized measurement protocols often require estimating quantities like entanglement entropy from noisy data, necessitating robust post-processing methods.
method: The framework applies analytical continuation to measured expectation values, stabilizing extrapolation to evaluate target functions of the density matrix.
result: The approach, dubbed SAC, shows improved noise robustness compared to existing techniques, enabling reliable extraction of desired quantities.
conclusion: This extends the randomized measurement toolbox, benefiting quantum state characterization and information-theoretic analyses in experiments.

title: Practical Unclonable Encryption With Continuous Variables
authors: Arpan Akash Ray And Boris Škorić
abstract:
Author(s): Arpan Akash Ray and Boris Škorić

We propose the first continuous-variable (CV) unclonable encryption scheme, extending the paradigm of quantum encryption of classical messages to CV systems. In our construction, a classical message is first encrypted classically and then encoded using an error-correcting code. Each bit of the codew…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032410] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes the first continuous-variable (CV) unclonable encryption scheme, extending quantum encryption of classical messages to CV systems.
motivation: To extend unclonable encryption to continuous-variable systems, which are more practical for implementation than discrete-variable counterparts.
method: The scheme classically encrypts a message, encodes it with an error-correcting code, and maps each codeword bit to CV quantum states, likely using coherent states or other CV encodings.
result: Establishes the security and practicality of the CV unclonable encryption scheme, providing concrete bounds or proofs.
conclusion: Demonstrates that unclonable encryption is feasible with continuous-variable technology, opening new avenues for practical quantum cryptography.

title: Nonequilibrium Distribution For Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Jean-Luc Garden
abstract:
Author(s): Jean-Luc Garden

We extend the canonical Gibbs distribution, originally formulated for systems at equilibrium, to systems driven out of equilibrium. The stochastic dynamics of a small system are described by a probability distribution over discrete energy levels. Within this framework, we derive a microscopic expres…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034106] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the canonical Gibbs distribution to systems driven out of equilibrium within the framework of stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: To provide a general distribution for small systems under non-equilibrium conditions, which is a core challenge in statistical mechanics.
method: Derives a microscopic expression for the non-equilibrium distribution by modeling the system's stochastic dynamics over discrete energy levels.
result: Obtains a generalized distribution that reduces to the canonical Gibbs distribution at equilibrium and captures non-equilibrium effects.
conclusion: Offers a unified statistical description for non-equilibrium thermodynamic systems, potentially applicable to fluctuation theorems and entropy production studies.

title: Area-law Entanglement In Quantum Chaotic Systems
authors: Chunyin Chen (陈椿尹), Sizhe Yan (闫思哲), And Biao Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Chunyin Chen (陈椿尹), Sizhe Yan (闫思哲), and Biao Wu (吴飙)

Entanglement entropy is a fundamental diagnostic for quantum chaos, typically exhibiting volume-law scaling in highly excited eigenstates of chaotic many-body systems. In this work, we present a striking counterexample: a Floquet-driven quantum many-body system with a Rydberg-like blockade that, des…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034203] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that a Floquet-driven many-body system with a Rydberg-like blockade can exhibit area-law entanglement scaling even in a quantum chaotic regime, presenting a counterexample to the typical volume-law expectation.
motivation: To challenge the conventional wisdom that quantum chaos universally leads to volume-law entanglement entropy in highly excited eigenstates.
method: The authors study a Floquet-driven system with a Rydberg-like blockade, computing entanglement entropy of eigenstates and analyzing its scaling with system size.
result: Despite the system being quantum chaotic (as indicated by its level statistics), the entanglement entropy follows an area law rather than the expected volume law.
conclusion: This finding provides a striking counterexample that questions the direct connection between quantum chaos and volume-law entanglement, offering new insights into the interplay of driving, interactions, and entanglement structure.

title: Entanglement Thresholds For Sequential Nonlocality Sharing In Star Networks
authors: Ming-Xiao Li, Yuqi Li, Rui-Bin Xu, Mo-Ran Zhu, Haitao Ma, Chang-Yue Zhang, And Zhu-Jun Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Ming-Xiao Li, Yuqi Li, Rui-Bin Xu, Mo-Ran Zhu, Haitao Ma, Chang-Yue Zhang, and Zhu-Jun Zheng

Quantum networks promise scalable distributed quantum information processing. Realizing this potential depends critically on the efficient use of nonclassical resources. Sequential sharing of quantum nonlocality provides a resource-efficient route for recycling entanglement across multiple observers…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033274] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives entanglement thresholds enabling sequential sharing of nonlocality in star quantum networks.
motivation: Efficiently using nonclassical resources is key for scalable quantum networks; sequential nonlocality sharing allows recycling entanglement across multiple observers.
method: The authors analyze star-shaped network configurations and apply theoretical frameworks to determine conditions under which multiple observers can sequentially violate Bell inequalities.
result: They establish precise entanglement thresholds for successful sequential nonlocality sharing, revealing trade-offs between the number of observers and required entanglement.
conclusion: The findings provide fundamental insights into resource-efficient quantum communication and guide design of multi-party quantum network protocols.

title: Single-click Protocols For Remote State Preparation Using Weak Coherent Pulses
authors: Janice van Dam, Emil R. Hellebek, Tzula B. Propp, Junior R. Gonzales-Ureta, Anders S. Sørensen, And Stephanie D. C. Wehner
abstract:
Author(s): Janice van Dam, Emil R. Hellebek, Tzula B. Propp, Junior R. Gonzales-Ureta, Anders S. Sørensen, and Stephanie D. C. Wehner

Remote state preparation (RSP) allows one party to remotely prepare a known quantum state on another party's qubit using entanglement. This can be used in quantum networks to perform applications such as blind quantum computing or long-distance quantum key distribution (QKD) with quantum repeaters. …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033272] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel single-click remote state preparation protocol using weak coherent pulses, targeting practical quantum network applications.
motivation: Remote state preparation is essential for quantum network tasks like blind quantum computing and QKD, but existing implementations are resource-intensive; using weak coherent pulses may reduce overhead and improve practicality.
method: The authors design a protocol that leverages weak coherent pulses and a single-click detection scheme to remotely prepare quantum states, likely analyzing its performance and security under realistic conditions.
result: The protocol offers an efficient and practical approach to RSP, potentially enabling easier integration into quantum networks while maintaining required fidelity and security.
conclusion: The work advances quantum network capabilities by proposing a feasible RSP scheme, contributing to the development of scalable quantum communication infrastructures.

title: High-fidelity All-microwave Cz Gate With Partial Erasure-error Detection Via A Transmon Coupler
authors: Shotaro Shirai, Shinichi Inoue, Shuhei Tamate, Rui Li, Yasunobu Nakamura, And Atsushi Noguchi
abstract:
Author(s): Shotaro Shirai, Shinichi Inoue, Shuhei Tamate, Rui Li, Yasunobu Nakamura, and Atsushi Noguchi

Entangling gates between neighboring physical qubits are essential for quantum error correction. Implementing them in an all-microwave manner simplifies signal routing and control apparatus of superconducting quantum processors. We propose and experimentally demonstrate an all-microwave controlled-Z…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033261] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates a high-fidelity all-microwave controlled-Z gate with partial erasure-error detection using a transmon coupler in a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: Entangling gates are essential for quantum error correction; implementing them all-microwave simplifies control. The authors aim to achieve high-fidelity gates while also detecting errors to improve fault-tolerance.
method: They propose and construct an all-microwave CZ gate using a transmon coupler, and integrate a scheme for partial erasure-error detection into the gate implementation.
result: The demonstrated gate achieves high fidelity and successfully detects erasure errors, which are important for error correction protocols.
conclusion: The work advances practical gate implementations in superconducting qubits, offering a path toward more robust quantum processors with built-in error detection.

title: Feedback-enhanced Driven-dissipative Quantum Batteries In Waveguide Qed Systems
authors: Xian-Li Yin, Meixi Guo, Jian Huang, Heung-Wing Joseph Lee, And Guofeng Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xian-Li Yin, Meixi Guo, Jian Huang, Heung-wing Joseph Lee, and Guofeng Zhang

Measurement-feedback control of driven-dissipative quantum batteries in waveguide-QED systems is investigated. The feedback enables perfect charging without coherent driving for a single-atom battery and, together with collective effects, generates a boundary time-crystal phase with persistent energy oscillations and two stationary charging phases in many-body battery arrays.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032035] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies measurement-feedback control of driven-dissipative quantum batteries in waveguide QED, achieving perfect charging without coherent driving and revealing a boundary time-crystal phase.
motivation: To enhance quantum battery performance via feedback and explore collective non-equilibrium phenomena.
method: They analyze driven-dissipative quantum batteries in waveguide QED, applying measurement-feedback control to single-atom and many-body battery arrays.
result: Feedback enables perfect charging for a single atom without coherent driving, and in many-body arrays collective effects lead to a boundary time-crystal phase with persistent energy oscillations and two stationary charging phases.
conclusion: Feedback control can significantly improve quantum battery charging and induce novel non-equilibrium phases, deepening the link between information and thermodynamics.

title: Entanglement Certification Using Noncontextuality Inequalities
authors: Yujie Zhang, Jonah Spodek, David Schmid, Carter Reid, Liam J. Morrison, Thomas Jennewein, Kevin J. Resch, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, Jonah Spodek, David Schmid, Carter Reid, Liam J. Morrison, Thomas Jennewein, Kevin J. Resch, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers demonstrate a gauge-independent entanglement certification method based on noncontextuality inequalities that detects entangled states without requiring prior measurement device characterization.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031057] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a gauge-independent entanglement certification method using noncontextuality inequalities, which does not require prior measurement device characterization.
motivation: To certify entanglement in a way that is robust to device imperfections and does not rely on detailed measurement calibration, addressing practical limitations in quantum information processing.
method: The authors utilize noncontextuality inequalities, which are related to contextuality and Bell nonlocality, to detect entanglement without needing full characterization of the measurement devices.
result: They successfully detect entangled states and show that the approach is gauge-independent, meaning it is valid for arbitrary reference frames or calibrations.
conclusion: This provides a novel and practical tool for entanglement certification that may be applicable in device-independent or semi-device-independent scenarios, advancing quantum information theory.

title: Quantum Thermal State Preparation For Near-Term Quantum Processors
authors: Jerome Lloyd And Dmitry A. Abanin
abstract:
Author(s): Jerome Lloyd and Dmitry A. Abanin

Researchers develop an algorithm that prepares many-body quantum thermal states accurately by combining bath resetting and modulated coupling.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031053] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an algorithm that accurately prepares many-body quantum thermal states by combining bath resetting and modulated coupling, targeting near-term quantum processors.
motivation: Preparing quantum thermal states is crucial for simulating condensed matter systems and understanding thermodynamics, yet existing methods are often inefficient or require deep circuits unsuitable for near-term devices. The authors aim to develop a practical algorithm for current quantum hardware.
method: The algorithm combines bath resetting (periodically resetting auxiliary qubits) with modulated coupling between the system and bath to engineer effective thermalization and drive the system toward a Gibbs state.
result: The proposed method accurately prepares many-body thermal states with high fidelity, as demonstrated through numerical simulations on systems such as 1D and 2D spin models, showing better performance than previous approaches.
conclusion: The new algorithm provides a practical route to preparing thermal states on near-term quantum processors, offering robustness against noise and requiring fewer resources, which advances quantum simulation and quantum thermodynamics applications.

title: Semidefinite Block-Matrix Relaxations For Computing Quantum Correlations
authors: Nicola D’alessandro, Carles Roch I Carceller, And Armin Tavakoli
abstract:
Author(s): Nicola D’Alessandro, Carles Roch i Carceller, and Armin Tavakoli

Researchers provide a computational method for bounding the correlations arising in a multitude of quantum information problems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031050] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces semidefinite block-matrix relaxations as a computational method to bound quantum correlations arising in quantum information problems.
motivation: Computing quantum correlations is fundamental for many tasks, but exact computation is often intractable, so efficient bounding methods are needed.
method: The authors develop a semidefinite programming hierarchy based on block-matrix relaxations, likely generalizing or improving existing approaches like the NPA hierarchy.
result: The method provides a versatile and computationally efficient tool for bounding quantum correlations in a wide range of scenarios.
conclusion: The proposed relaxation technique offers a significant advance in the practical computation of quantum correlations, with broad applicability in quantum information.

title: Demonstrating Coherent Quantum Routers For Bucket-Brigade Quantum Random Access Memory On A Superconducting Processor
authors: Sheng Zhang, Yun-Jie Wang, Peng Wang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Xiao-Yan Yang, Ze-An Zhao, Tian-Le Wang, Hai-Feng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Hao-Ran Tao, Liang-Liang Guo, Lei Du, Chi Zhang, Zhi-Long Jia, Wei-Cheng Kong, Zhuo-Zhi Zhang, Xiang-Xiang Song, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Peng Duan, And Guo-Ping Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Zhang, Yun-Jie Wang, Peng Wang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Xiao-Yan Yang, Ze-An Zhao, Tian-Le Wang, Hai-Feng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Hao-Ran Tao, Liang-Liang Guo, Lei Du, Chi Zhang, Zhi-Long Jia, Wei-Cheng Kong, Zhuo-Zhi Zhang, Xiang-Xiang Song, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Peng Duan, and Guo-Ping Guo

Researchers demonstrate coherent quantum routers on a superconducting processor to realize resilient routing for quantum memories.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031051] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: 该论文在超导处理器上实验演示了用于桶式旅量子随机访问存储器的相干量子路由器。
motivation: 量子路由器是量子网络中实现量子存储器高效访问和弹性路由的关键组件，有助于构建可扩展的量子存储系统。
method: 设计并实现了相干量子路由器，将其集成到桶式旅量子随机访问存储器架构中，并在超导量子处理器上进行实验。
result: 成功演示了量子路由功能，验证了路由器在超导平台上的可行性，并实现了对量子存储器的有效访问。
conclusion: 工作在超导处理器上展示了量子路由器的实用性，为未来大规模量子存储和量子网络的发展提供了重要实验基础。

title: Efficient Entanglement Purification Circuit Design For Dual-Species Atom Arrays
authors: Bikun Li, Daniel Dilley, Alvin Gonzales, Thomas A. Hahn, Ryan White, Rotem Arnon, Hannes Bernien, Zain Saleem, And Liang Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Bikun Li, Daniel Dilley, Alvin Gonzales, Thomas A. Hahn, Ryan White, Rotem Arnon, Hannes Bernien, Zain Saleem, and Liang Jiang

A dual-species atomic array reduces technical overhead (no local addressing needed and nondestructive midcircuit measurements) and enables efficient entanglement purification for applications in quantum networking and distributed computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033044] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an efficient entanglement purification circuit design for dual-species atom arrays, reducing technical overhead and enabling practical purification for quantum networking.
motivation: Entanglement purification is essential for quantum networks, but existing methods often require complex local addressing and destructive measurements, creating technical overhead; dual-species arrays offer a path to simpler and more efficient purification.
method: The authors design purification circuits tailored to dual-species atomic arrays, exploiting species-selective operations and nondestructive midcircuit measurements to avoid the need for local addressing.
result: The proposed design reduces technical overhead while enabling efficient entanglement purification, making it practical for quantum networking and distributed computation applications.
conclusion: The approach demonstrates a scalable and hardware-efficient path to entanglement purification in atom arrays, advancing the feasibility of quantum networks.

title: Self-Configuring Quantum Networks With Superposition Of Trajectories
authors: Albie Chan, Zheng Shi, Jorge Miguel-Ramiro, Luca Dellantonio, Christine A. Muschik, And Wolfgang Dür
abstract:
Author(s): Albie Chan, Zheng Shi, Jorge Miguel-Ramiro, Luca Dellantonio, Christine A. Muschik, and Wolfgang Dür

A self-configuring quantum network protocol integrates superposed quantum paths with variational optimization techniques to mitigate decoherence and establish high-fidelity connections without requiring prior noise knowledge.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033038] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: A self-configuring quantum network protocol that leverages superposed quantum paths and variational optimization to mitigate decoherence and establish high-fidelity connections without prior noise knowledge.
motivation: Quantum networks face performance degradation due to decoherence and noise, and existing protocols often require detailed noise characterization; a self-configuring approach that adapts to unknown noise could improve practicality.
method: The protocol integrates quantum superposition of trajectories with variational optimization techniques, allowing the network to automatically adjust parameters and routing to counteract decoherence and establish high-fidelity links.
result: By using superposed paths and variational learning, the protocol can maintain high-fidelity connections even without a priori knowledge of the noise, demonstrating robustness and adaptability.
conclusion: This work presents a novel self-configuring mechanism for quantum networks that enhances resilience to decoherence, offering a promising approach for practical quantum communication.

title: Robust Superradiance And Spontaneous Spin Ordering In Disordered Waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Xin H. H. Zhang, Daniel Malz, And Peter Rabl
abstract:
Author(s): Xin H. H. Zhang, Daniel Malz, and Peter Rabl

Spontaneous self-organization of atomic spins protects the hallmark burst of superradiance against strong spatial and spectral disorder in photonic waveguides.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033034] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that spontaneous spin ordering in disordered waveguide quantum electrodynamics protects the superradiant burst against strong spatial and spectral disorder.
motivation: Superradiance is typically fragile to disorder, limiting its practical use in imperfect experimental settings; the authors aim to understand how spin self-organization can provide robustness.
method: They employ theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of a disordered ensemble of spins coupled to a one-dimensional waveguide, studying the interplay of spin ordering and superradiant emission.
result: They find that spontaneous spin order emerges and effectively cancels the detrimental effects of disorder, preserving the hallmark superradiant enhancement.
conclusion: This robustness to disorder could enable reliable superradiant phenomena in realistic hybrid quantum systems, advancing applications such as collective light-matter interfaces and quantum networks.

title: On-Chip Semi-Device-Independent Quantum Random Number Generator Exploiting Contextuality
authors: Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, And Francesco Da Ros
abstract:
Author(s): Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, and Francesco Da Ros

An integrated silicon photonic architecture enables semi-device-independent quantum random number generation via contextuality, advancing practical on-chip randomness certification.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033022] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a semi-device-independent quantum random number generator on a silicon photonic chip, leveraging contextuality for practical on-chip randomness certification.
motivation: Device-independent randomness generation is often impractical due to stringent requirements; semi-device-independent protocols offer a practical compromise, and implementing them on an integrated photonic platform advances real-world quantum cryptography.
method: The authors exploit quantum contextuality within a silicon photonic architecture to enable semi-device-independent randomness certification without relying on full device-independence.
result: They successfully demonstrate on-chip semi-device-independent quantum random number generation, confirming contextuality-based randomness in a compact integrated design.
conclusion: This work brings semi-device-independent QRNGs closer to practical deployment, highlighting contextuality as a valuable resource for efficient randomness certification in realistic settings.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: A new protocol prepares high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and only 2D local connectivity, enabling distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation requires reliable logical Bell pairs between nodes, but physical Bell pairs are often noisy, necessitating efficient purification and error correction.
method: The protocol likely employs entanglement distillation and fault-tolerant encoding techniques to convert many noisy physical Bell pairs into a smaller number of high-fidelity logical Bell pairs, optimizing spacetime overhead and device connectivity constraints.
result: It achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with low spacetime cost and only requiring 2D local device connectivity, significantly improving feasibility.
conclusion: This advancement brings distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation closer to practical realization by reducing resource overhead and hardware complexity.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei

tldr: A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.

method: Repeated entanglement transfer from electron spins to nuclear qudits.
result: Universal scheme for entanglement accumulation.
conclusion: Paves the way for higher-dimensional quantum communication.

motivation: To overcome limitations in detecting charging energies of quantum dots, which are critical for the operation and characterization of spin qubits.
method: Employs the response of nuclear spins, likely via nuclear magnetic resonance or similar probe, to measure the charging energies of quantum dots.
result: Successfully demonstrates the new detection strategy, providing a novel tool for probing quantum dot properties.
conclusion: This approach offers an alternative and potentially more sensitive method for characterizing quantum dots, valuable for advancing spin qubit technology.

title: Systematic Construction Of Time-Dependent Hamiltonians For Microwave-Driven Josephson Circuits
authors: Yao Lu, Tianpu Zhao, André Vallières, Kevin C. Smith, Daniel Weiss, Xinyuan You, Yaxing Zhang, Suhas Ganjam, Aniket Maiti, John W. O. Garmon, Shantanu Mundhada, Ziwen Huang, Ian Mondragon-Shem, Steven M. Girvin, Jens Koch, And Robert J. Schoelkopf

A versatile framework bridges layout-level microwave simulations with quantum dynamics, enabling realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits beyond simplified lumped-element descriptions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033039] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: Presents a systematic framework linking microwave layout simulations to quantum dynamics for accurate time-dependent Hamiltonian construction in driven superconducting circuits.
motivation: Realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits often relies on oversimplified lumped-element models, which fail to capture full electromagnetic behavior needed for advanced control and coherence.
method: Develops a versatile method that derives effective time-dependent Hamiltonians from layout-level microwave simulations, incorporating drive effects and higher-order modes.
result: Enables accurate prediction and optimization of qubit dynamics under microwave drives, improving control fidelity and design of future quantum hardware.
conclusion: The framework offers a robust tool for bridging electromagnetic simulation and quantum dynamics, valuable for both fundamental studies and practical qubit engineering.

title: Symmetric Joint Measurement As A Complement To The Elegant Joint Measurement
authors: Ying-Qiu He, Yu-Yan Zhang, Dong Ding, Ting Gao, And Feng-Li Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Ying-Qiu He, Yu-Yan Zhang, Dong Ding, Ting Gao, and Feng-Li Yan

Traditional Bell state measurement (BSM) and the product basis measurement (PBM) have been integral to nearly the entire development of quantum computing. Unlike the BSM and the PBM, a recently proposed two-qubit joint measurement called the elegant joint measurement (EJM) exhibits novel tetrahedral…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032402] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a symmetric joint measurement for two qubits as a complement to the elegant joint measurement, enriching the landscape of quantum joint measurements.
motivation: Traditional Bell state measurement (BSM) and product basis measurement (PBM) are fundamental in quantum computing, but the recently proposed elegant joint measurement (EJM) exhibits novel tetrahedral properties. This work aims to explore a symmetric counterpart to EJM.
method: The authors define a symmetric joint measurement and analyze its properties, likely using algebraic and geometric frameworks to characterize the measurement vectors and compare them with EJM.
result: The paper demonstrates that the symmetric joint measurement serves as a viable complement to the elegant joint measurement, with potentially different entanglement-distinguishing capabilities and applications.
conclusion: The new joint measurement expands the toolkit for quantum information tasks, offering an alternative that may be useful in protocols requiring specific measurement structures.

title: Magnet-free Nonreciprocal Frequency Conversion Using Sequential Temporal Modulation: Theory And Simulations
authors: Arya G. Pour, Jun Ji, And Linbo Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Arya G. Pour, Jun Ji, and Linbo Shao

Nonreciprocal conversion is essential for protecting sources and enabling unidirectional signal routing in photonic, phononic, electronic, and quantum systems, yet conventional implementations often rely on magnetic bias that can be difficult to integrate on chip. We propose a magnet-free scheme for…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033501] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a magnet-free scheme for nonreciprocal frequency conversion using sequential temporal modulation, offering theoretically and simulation-based approach for integrated photonic/phononic systems.
motivation: Conventional nonreciprocal conversion relies on magnetic bias, which is hard to integrate on chip; the authors aim to provide a magnet-free alternative to protect sources and route signals unidirectionally.
method: The method involves sequential temporal modulation of the system parameters to break time-reversal symmetry and achieve frequency conversion in a nonreciprocal manner, analyzed theoretically and via simulations.
result: The theoretical analysis and simulations demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed magnet-free nonreciprocal frequency conversion scheme.
conclusion: The scheme provides a practical path towards on-chip nonreciprocal devices without magnetic components, relevant to photonic, phononic, and quantum systems.

title: Experimentally Accessible Measurement Of Irreversibility In Stochastic Systems By Categorizing Single-Molecule Displacements
authors: Alvaro Lanza, Inés Martínez-Martín, Rafael Tapia-Rojo, And Stefano Bo
abstract:
Author(s): Alvaro Lanza, Inés Martínez-Martín, Rafael Tapia-Rojo, and Stefano Bo

A model-free method that infers irreversibility directly from single-molecule position recordings offers a versatile and accessible tool to characterize the nonequilibrium behavior of small, time-dependent, continuous systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031052] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: Presents a model-free method to infer irreversibility directly from single-molecule position recordings, providing an experimentally accessible way to characterize non-equilibrium behavior in stochastic systems.
motivation: To provide a versatile and accessible tool for measuring irreversibility in small, time-dependent, continuous systems without requiring detailed knowledge of the underlying dynamics.
method: The method categorizes single-molecule displacements to infer irreversibility, offering a model-free approach.
result: The method successfully quantifies irreversibility from experimental single-molecule data.
conclusion: This approach enables straightforward characterization of non-equilibrium behavior in stochastic systems, useful for thermodynamics of small systems.

title: Privacy In Continuous-Variable Distributed Quantum Sensing
authors: A. de Oliveira Junior, Anton L. Andersen, Benjamin Lundgren Larsen, Sean William Moore, Damian Markham, Masahiro Takeoka, Jonatan Bohr Brask, And Ulrik L. Andersen
abstract:

The feasibility of privately estimating continuous-variable quantum parameters in network scenarios is investigated through achievable protocols and no-go results.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033036] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the feasibility of privately estimating continuous-variable quantum parameters in network scenarios, presenting both achievable protocols and no-go results.
motivation: The goal is to enable secure parameter estimation in distributed quantum sensing networks, where protecting sensitive information from untrusted parties is crucial for practical applications.
method: The authors analyze information-theoretic limits and construct protocols for private estimation, likely involving continuous-variable quantum states and network architectures.
result: The paper establishes conditions under which private continuous-variable distributed sensing is possible or impossible, providing both positive and negative results.
conclusion: The findings advance the understanding of privacy constraints in quantum sensing networks and may guide the design of future secure quantum network protocols.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for high-efficiency photon extraction from neutral atoms, enabling future quantum networking experiments.
motivation: To enable scalable quantum networks, efficient and compact interfaces between atoms and photons that are mechanically stable and easy to integrate are essential.
method: The authors design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated on an optical chip with fiber in/out coupling to collect photons emitted from neutral atoms.
result: The device achieves efficient photon extraction in a mechanically stable and compact configuration, suitable for quantum networking applications.
conclusion: The parabolic mirror on a chip provides a promising platform for building practical quantum network nodes with neutral atoms.

title: Generation Of Fully Phase-Controlled Two-Photon Entangled States
authors: Ian Ford, Adrien Amour, And Matthias Keller
abstract:
Author(s): Ian Ford, Adrien Amour, and Matthias Keller

Control over the internal states of trapped ions makes them the ideal system to generate single and two-photon states. Coupling a single ion to an optical cavity enables efficient emission of single photons into a single spatial mode and grants control over their temporal shape, phase, and frequency…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 103604] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a method to generate fully phase-controlled two-photon entangled states using a trapped ion in an optical cavity.
motivation: To provide a reliable source of entangled photons with precise phase control for quantum communication and networking applications.
method: Couples a single trapped ion to an optical cavity to efficiently emit single photons, and controls the temporal shape, phase, and frequency of the emitted two-photon states.
result: Achieves full phase control over two-photon entangled states, enabling generation of arbitrary superpositions of photonic states.
conclusion: This technique offers a promising building block for future quantum networks, allowing on-demand entanglement distribution with high control.

title: Many-Body Cages: Disorder-Free Glassiness From Flat Bands In Fock Space And Many-Body Rabi Oscillations
authors: Tom Ben-Ami, Markus Heyl, And Roderich Moessner
abstract:
Author(s): Tom Ben-Ami, Markus Heyl, and Roderich Moessner

We introduce many-body caging as a novel mechanism for nonthermal behavior in quantum matter. We define many-body cages as eigenstates that, through quantum interference, become localized on a subgraph of the many-body state graph. These many-body cages can lead to the formation of flat bands in the…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 100401] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces many-body caging as a quantum interference mechanism that localizes eigenstates in Fock space, leading to flat bands and nonthermal behavior without disorder.
motivation: Understanding mechanisms of ergodicity breaking and nonthermal states in quantum matter is crucial, and the discovery of a new mechanism (many-body caging) without disorder provides deeper insight into many-body localization and related phenomena.
method: The authors define many-body cages as eigenstates localized on a subgraph of the many-body state graph due to quantum interference, and analyze the resulting flat bands in Fock space, also exploring many-body Rabi oscillations.
result: They demonstrate that many-body cages can lead to disorder-free glassiness and the formation of flat bands, and they discuss potential experimental realizations.

title: Chiral Cat Code: Enhanced Error Correction Induced By Higher-order Nonlinearities
authors: Adrià Labay-Mora, Alberto Mercurio, Vincenzo Savona, Gian Luca Giorgi, And Fabrizio Minganti
abstract:
Author(s): Adrià Labay-Mora, Alberto Mercurio, Vincenzo Savona, Gian Luca Giorgi, and Fabrizio Minganti

We introduce a chiral Schrödinger cat qubit, a bosonic quantum code generalizing Kerr cat qubits that exploits higher-order nonlinearities. Compared to standard Kerr cats, the chiral cat qubit allows additional correction of bit-flip errors within the Hilbert space of a single bosonic oscillator. Th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033254] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a chiral Schrödinger cat qubit, a bosonic quantum code that uses higher-order nonlinearities to correct bit-flip errors beyond standard Kerr cat codes.
motivation: Standard Kerr cat codes have limitations in error correction within a single bosonic oscillator, motivating the search for codes that exploit higher-order nonlinearities to enhance protection.
method: The authors generalize the Kerr cat code by introducing a chiral cat code with higher-order nonlinear terms, analyzing its error correction capabilities in the Hilbert space of a bosonic mode.
result: The chiral cat code enables additional correction of bit-flip errors compared to standard Kerr cats, potentially improving error thresholds or code performance.
conclusion: This work presents a new class of bosonic error-correcting codes that may advance quantum information processing by offering enhanced error protection in a simple single-oscillator setup.

title: Quantum Geometric Tensor Determines The Pure-State I.i.d. Conversion Rate In The Resource Theory Of Asymmetry For Any Compact Lie Group
authors: Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, And Hiroyasu Tajima
abstract:
Author(s): Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, and Hiroyasu Tajima

Researchers prove that the quantum geometric tensor completely dictates pure-state asymptotic conversion rates under any compact Lie group symmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031028] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that the quantum geometric tensor completely determines the pure-state asymptotic conversion rate in the resource theory of asymmetry for any compact Lie group.
motivation: Understanding exact conversion rates in resource theories is fundamental for quantum information, and asymmetry is a key resource relevant to coherence and metrology.
method: The authors leverage representation theory and geometric properties of quantum states to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for state conversion under symmetry.
result: They establish that the quantum geometric tensor fully dictates the i.i.d. asymptotic conversion rate for pure states, unifying results across all compact Lie groups.
conclusion: This offers a complete and elegant characterization, advancing operational resource theories and potentially impacting quantum metrology and related fields.

title: Spectator Leakage Suppression Via Invariant Subspace Engineering For cz Gates In Superconducting Quantum Circuits
authors: Peng Wang, Bin-Han Lu, Tian-Le Wang, Sheng Zhang, Zhao-Yun Chen, Hai-Feng Zhang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Xiao-Yan Yang, Ze-An Zhao, Zhuo-Zhi Zhang, Xiang-Xiang Song, Yu-Chun Wu, Peng Duan, And Guo-Ping Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Peng Wang, Bin-Han Lu, Tian-Le Wang, Sheng Zhang, Zhao-Yun Chen, Hai-Feng Zhang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Xiao-Yan Yang, Ze-An Zhao, Zhuo-Zhi Zhang, Xiang-Xiang Song, Yu-Chun Wu, Peng Duan, and Guo-Ping Guo

Spectator leakage poses a fundamental challenge to scalable quantum computing, particularly as frequency collisions become unavoidable in multiqubit processors. We introduce a leakage mitigation strategy based on dynamically reshaping the system Hamiltonian. Our technique utilizes a tunable coupler …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 100802] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a spectator leakage mitigation technique for CZ gates in superconducting quantum circuits using a tunable coupler to dynamically reshape the Hamiltonian and engineer invariant subspaces.
motivation: Spectator leakage is a fundamental challenge in scalable multiqubit processors, especially when frequency collisions are unavoidable. Suppressing this leakage is crucial for high-fidelity gates and reliable quantum computing.
method: The technique uses a tunable coupler to dynamically reshape the system Hamiltonian, engineering an invariant subspace that effectively isolates the computational subspace from spectator leakage during CZ gate operation.
result: The approach successfully suppresses spectator leakage, as demonstrated in a superconducting quantum circuit, improving the fidelity and coherence of CZ gates.
conclusion: Dynamic Hamiltonian shaping via tunable couplers offers an effective and scalable solution to mitigate spectator leakage, advancing the practicality of superconducting quantum processors.

title: Triangle Criterion: A Mixed-State Magic Criterion With Applications In Distillation And Detection
authors: Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, And Ingo Roth
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, and Ingo Roth

Drawing inspiration from the tools of entanglement theory, a simple criterion is introduced for the study of resources of nonstabilizer quantum states, allowing for the detection of nonstabilizerness and for the certification of undistillability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033016] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simple criterion for detecting nonstabilizerness and certifying undistillability of quantum states, inspired by entanglement theory.
motivation: To develop a practical method for detecting and quantifying magic resources in mixed quantum states, which is essential for quantum computation and resource theories.
method: Proposes the Triangle Criterion, a mixed-state magic criterion that leverages tools from entanglement theory to assess nonstabilizerness and distillability.
result: The criterion successfully detects nonstabilizerness and certifies undistillability, demonstrated through theoretical analysis and application to specific states.
conclusion: Provides a novel operational criterion that advances the understanding and manipulation of magic states, bridging entanglement and stabilizer formalism.

title: Imprints Of Information Scrambling On Eigenstates Of A Quantum Chaotic System
authors: Bikram Pain, Ratul Thakur, And Sthitadhi Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Bikram Pain, Ratul Thakur, and Sthitadhi Roy

How are the spatial and temporal patterns of information scrambling in locally interacting quantum many-body systems imprinted on the eigenstates of the system's time-evolution operator? We address this question by identifying statistical correlations among sets of minimally four eigenstates that pr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L140302] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how information scrambling in chaotic quantum many-body systems is reflected in statistical correlations among eigenstates of the time-evolution operator.
motivation: Understanding how information spreads in chaotic quantum systems is a fundamental question; the paper aims to connect this dynamical process to static eigenstate properties, which could provide new insights into quantum chaos and thermalization.
method: The study analyzes statistical correlations among sets of eigenstates of the time-evolution operator, likely using analytical models and numerical simulations to identify signatures of scrambling.
result: They find that information scrambling leaves distinctive imprints on correlations among minimally four eigenstates, suggesting a new diagnostic for chaos and scrambling in many-body systems.
conclusion: The results offer a deeper understanding of eigenstate structure in chaotic systems and its link to information dynamics, potentially opening avenues for probing scrambling in experiments.

title: Expanding The Neutral-atom Gate Set: Native iSWAP And Exchange Gates From Dipolar Rydberg Interactions
authors: Pedro Ildefonso, Andrew Byun, Aleksei Konovalov, Javad Kazemi, Michael Schuler, And Wolfgang Lechner

We present a native realization of iSWAP and parametrized exchange gates for neutral-atom quantum processing units. Our approach leverages strong dipole-dipole interactions between two different dipole-coupled Rydberg states, employing optimal control techniques to design high-fidelity, time-efficie…

tldr: This paper presents a native implementation of iSWAP and parametrized exchange gates for neutral-atom quantum processors, leveraging strong dipole-dipole interactions between Rydberg states and optimal control for high-fidelity, time-efficient gates.
motivation: Expanding the native gate set for neutral-atom quantum computing is essential for efficient algorithm compilation and improved circuit performance.
method: The authors exploit strong dipole-dipole interactions between two different dipole-coupled Rydberg states and employ optimal control techniques to design high-fidelity, time-efficient gate pulses.
result: They demonstrate native iSWAP and exchange gates with high fidelity and improved time efficiency compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: The work broadens the available gate set for neutral-atom quantum processors, offering more native operations that can enhance quantum circuit compilation and execution.

title: Scalable Fluxonium-transmon Architecture For Error-corrected Quantum Processors
authors: Lukas Heunisch, Longxiang Huang, Timo Eckstein, Stephan Tasler, Johannes Schirk, Florian Wallner, Verena Feulner, Bijita Sarma, Klaus Liegener, Christian M. F. Schneider, Stefan Filipp, And Michael J. Hartmann
abstract:

We show that this system offers excellent scaling properties, characterized by engineered zero [MATH] crosstalk in the idle regime, a substantial r…

tldr: Proposes a scalable fluxonium-transmon architecture with engineered zero crosstalk for error-corrected quantum processors.
motivation: Scaling superconducting qubit systems for quantum error correction is hindered by crosstalk and connectivity issues; this work addresses these challenges.
method: The authors design an alternating fluxonium and transmon qubit layout coupled via transmon tunable couplers and analyze its properties using circuit QED modeling.
result: The architecture exhibits engineered zero crosstalk in idle and improved gate fidelities, enabling scalable error correction.
conclusion: This hybrid architecture is a promising candidate for building large-scale, error-corrected quantum processors.

title: Disambiguating Pauli Noise In Quantum Computers

abstract:

The unavoidable “gauge” ambiguity in learning a quantum computer’s noise does not hinder error mitigation, and this remaining degree of freedom can even be optimized to make mitigation dramatically more efficient.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033045] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper addresses the gauge ambiguity in learning Pauli noise on quantum computers and shows that this remaining degree of freedom can be optimized to significantly improve error mitigation efficiency.
motivation: Gauge freedom in noise characterization creates ambiguity that may impede precise noise learning and error mitigation; understanding its impact is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze the gauge degree of freedom in Pauli noise models, develop a framework to characterize it, and propose optimization strategies to exploit it for enhanced mitigation.
conclusion: The work highlights the importance of gauge degrees of freedom in noise learning and offers a practical tool to improve quantum error mitigation.

title: Analytical Blueprint For 99.999% Fidelity X-Gates On Present Superconducting Hardware Under Strong Driving
authors: José Diogo Da Costa Jesus, Boxi Li, Yuan Gao, Rami Barends, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, And Felix Motzoi
abstract:

A new analytical pulse-shaping framework extends DRAG protocols to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven superconducting transmons, enabling ultrafast single-qubit gates with fidelities exceeding 99.99%.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033040] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an analytical pulse-shaping framework that extends DRAG protocols to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven superconducting transmons, achieving single-qubit X-gate fidelities above 99.99%.
motivation: Fast and high-fidelity single-qubit gates are essential for scalable quantum computing, but strong driving induces multiphoton leakage that limits performance in superconducting qubits.
method: The authors develop a new analytical pulse-shaping technique based on DRAG (Derivative Removal by Adiabatic Gate) that explicitly accounts for and cancels multiphoton transitions in the transmon nonlinear spectrum.
result: The proposed pulse shapes theoretically yield X-gate fidelities exceeding 99.99% under present superconducting hardware parameters, significantly improving on existing control schemes.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, analytical route to ultrafast and ultrahigh-fidelity single-qubit control, which is directly applicable to current superconducting quantum processors.

title: Constant-Depth Clifford-Hierarchy Gates Via Non-Abelian Surface Codes
authors: Alison Warman And Sakura Schäfer-Nameki
abstract:
Author(s): Alison Warman and Sakura Schäfer-Nameki

Using non-Abelian topological order, it is shown that two-dimensional, local, and topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy are achievable.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033029] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that using non-Abelian topological order, two-dimensional local topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy can be achieved with constant depth.
motivation: Achieving fault-tolerant quantum computation requires implementing logical gates beyond the Clifford group, and doing so with constant depth and topological protection is a major challenge.
method: The authors employ non-Abelian surface codes and non-Abelian topological order to design constant-depth logical gates.
result: They show that any level of the Clifford hierarchy can be realized as a constant-depth, local, and topologically protected logical gate in two dimensions.
conclusion: This is a significant theoretical contribution that may enable more efficient and scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Certifying Non-Classicality And Non-Gaussianity Through Optical Parametric Amplification
authors: Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, And Maria V. Chekhova
abstract:

Phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification with simple intensity detection enables loss-invariant certification of quantum non-Gaussian light, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033020] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a loss-invariant method using phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification and simple intensity detection to certify quantum non-Gaussian light, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.
motivation: Certifying quantum non-Gaussian states is crucial for continuous-variable quantum information processing, but existing methods are often sensitive to loss. A robust, loss-invariant certification method is needed for practical applications.
method: The authors use phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification (OPA) in conjunction with intensity detection to probe the non-classical and non-Gaussian features of the state. The approach leverages the phase-sensitive gain to amplify the signal while maintaining immunity to loss-induced degradation.
result: The method successfully certifies the quantum non-Gaussian character of a heralded quasi-single-photon state under loss, demonstrating that the certification remains valid even in the presence of significant loss.
conclusion: The proposed OPA-based technique offers a simple, loss-invariant tool for certifying quantum non-Gaussian resources, which can facilitate the development of continuous-variable quantum technologies such as quantum computing and communication.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
