A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new strategy for magic-state cultivation on surface codes, achieving low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic states are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing but their preparation often has high overhead. The authors aim to reduce this overhead, particularly for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
method: The method likely involves using fold-transversal gates on surface codes to implement a cultivation protocol that leverages the connectivity constraints efficiently.
result: The new strategy achieves a lower spacetime overhead compared to existing methods, making magic-state cultivation more practical for certain quantum architectures.
conclusion: The work provides a promising pathway for efficient magic-state preparation in fault-tolerant quantum computers with nonlocal architectures, potentially accelerating progress towards practical quantum computing.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces twisted color circuits, a family of scalable fault-tolerant circuits for implementing non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code with nearest-neighbor couplings.
motivation: Scalable fault-tolerant quantum computation requires efficient implementation of non-Clifford gates, which is challenging on planar architectures.
method: They propose a family of circuit designs called twisted color circuits that use the 2D color code and achieve fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder.
result: The circuits enable universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings.
conclusion: The work provides a practical pathway for fault-tolerant quantum computation using color codes on planar hardware.

title: Two-Tooth Bosonic Quantum Comb For Temporal-Correlation Sensing
authors: Shaojiang Zhu, Xinyuan You, Alexander Romanenko, And Anna Grassellino
abstract:
Author(s): Shaojiang Zhu, Xinyuan You, Alexander Romanenko, and Anna Grassellino

We characterize the causal structure of coherence transport in open bosonic systems using a two-tooth quantum comb. We show that, by mapping sequential interactions between a structured bosonic absorber and a long-lived coherent probe onto a process-tensor description, the probe functions as a tempo…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 100403] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a two-tooth quantum comb to characterize the causal structure of coherence transport in open bosonic systems, mapping sequential interactions onto a process-tensor description.
motivation: To understand how coherence is transported in open quantum systems and to enable sensing of temporal correlations of the environment.
method: They use a two-tooth quantum comb and process-tensor formalism to describe sequential interactions between a structured bosonic absorber and a long-lived coherent probe.
result: The probe functions as a temporal-correlation sensor for the structured bosonic absorber, revealing the causal structure of coherence transport.
conclusion: The work provides a novel framework based on process tensors for characterizing coherence dynamics and sensing, relevant to quantum information processing and open system theory.

title: Close Encounters Between Periodic Light And Periodic Arrays Of Quantum Emitters
authors: Frieder Lindel, Carlos J. Sánchez Martínez, Johannes Feist, And Francisco J. García-Vidal
abstract:
Author(s): Frieder Lindel, Carlos J. Sánchez Martínez, Johannes Feist, and Francisco J. García-Vidal

We introduce crystal polaritons, hybrid excitations formed when the collective excitations of a periodic quantum-emitter array strongly couple to the resonant Bloch modes of a metasurface. This realizes a cavity-QED platform in which periodic light and periodic matter are treated on the same footing…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 103802] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: Introduces crystal polaritons as hybrid excitations from strong coupling between periodic quantum-emitter arrays and resonant Bloch modes of a metasurface, establishing a cavity-QED platform.
motivation: To address the interaction of periodic light with periodic matter on an equal footing, creating a new platform for strong light-matter coupling.
method: Theoretical analysis combining quantum-emitter arrays with metasurface modes, likely using a many-body quantum optics framework to treat the hybridized excitations.
result: Demonstrates the formation of crystal polaritons with controllable strong coupling, extending cavity-QED concepts to periodic systems.
conclusion: Provides a versatile platform for investigating photonic and matter periodicities, promising for quantum optics and information processing applications.

title: Complexity Of Quantum States In The Stabilizer Formalism
authors: Shuangshuang Fu, Shunlong Luo, And Yue Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Shuangshuang Fu, Shunlong Luo, and Yue Zhang

We initiate an investigation into a notion of state complexity for discrete-variable quantum systems. Specifically, we propose an information-theoretic quantifier for the complexity of quantum states within the stabilizer formalism of quantum computation. This is achieved by leveraging the symmetric…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032409] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an information-theoretic quantifier for the complexity of quantum states within the stabilizer formalism.
motivation: To develop a formal measure of state complexity in discrete-variable quantum systems, particularly for quantum computation contexts.
method: The authors propose a new complexity metric based on the stabilizer formalism, leveraging symmetric information-theoretic concepts.
result: They define a quantifier that captures the complexity of quantum states relative to stabilizer formalism.
conclusion: The work provides a novel tool for characterizing quantum states in quantum information and computation.

title: Reexamining The Role Of State Texture In Gate Identification And Fixed-point Resource Theories
authors: Alexander C. B. Greenwood, Joseph M. Lukens, Li Qian, And Brian T. Kirby
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander C. B. Greenwood, Joseph M. Lukens, Li Qian, and Brian T. Kirby

A protocol for identifying controlled-not (cnot) gates versus single-qubit-only gates in universal quantum circuits using randomized input states was recently shown to be intimately connected to the quantum resource of state texture. Here, we revisit this gate identification protocol and demonstrate…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032411] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits a gate identification protocol and its connection to the quantum resource of state texture, providing new analysis and insights.
motivation: To understand the role of state texture in identifying CNOT gates versus single-qubit gates in quantum circuits.
method: Reanalyzing the gate identification protocol through the lens of fixed-point resource theories.
result: Demonstrates that state texture plays a crucial role in the protocol, potentially refining previous understanding.
conclusion: State texture is a meaningful resource for gate identification tasks.

title: Quantum Coherence Dispersion
authors: Fernando Parisio
abstract:
Author(s): Fernando Parisio

We investigate the variability of the quantum coherences of an arbitrary density matrix, in a given basis. An easily computable quantity that captures this variability notion is proposed and a dual relationship with an appropriate entropy is observed, with coherence dispersion (CD) being maximized f…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032202] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a measure of the variability of quantum coherences in a fixed basis, termed coherence dispersion, and reveals its dual relationship with an entropy.
motivation: To quantify how spread out the off-diagonal elements of a density matrix are, providing a new perspective on coherence resources.
method: Proposes an easily computable quantity for coherence dispersion and analyzes its properties, including its connection to an appropriate entropy.
result: Demonstrates that coherence dispersion is maximized for certain states and establishes a duality with entropy.
conclusion: Offers a new tool for characterizing coherence in quantum systems.

title: Singular Value Transformation For Unknown Quantum Channels
authors: Ryotaro Niwa, Zane Marius Rossi, Philip Taranto, And Mio Murao
abstract:
Author(s): Ryotaro Niwa, Zane Marius Rossi, Philip Taranto, and Mio Murao

A universal method for block encoding the Liouville representation of quantum channels is presented, enabling the manipulation of the spectrum of unknown quantum channels.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L030401] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: Presents a universal method for block encoding the Liouville representation of quantum channels, enabling singular value transformation for unknown channels.
motivation: To manipulate the spectrum of unknown quantum channels, which is useful for various quantum information tasks.
method: Introduces a block encoding of the Liouville representation and applies singular value transformation to achieve the desired channel manipulation.
result: Provides a universal approach to process unknown quantum channels spectrally.
conclusion: This method broadens the toolbox for quantum channel processing.

title: Maximum-precision Charging Of Multiqubit Quantum Batteries
authors: Davide Rinaldi, Radim Filip, Dario Gerace, And Giacomo Guarnieri
abstract:
Author(s): Davide Rinaldi, Radim Filip, Dario Gerace, and Giacomo Guarnieri

Quantum batteries need precision-focused charging protocols to provide reliable quantum advantage. The authors borrow a technique from quantum thermodynamics to demonstrate that a sequential multi-qubit quantum battery can be charged with high precision, even in the presence of non-idealized working conditions, by exploiting specific quantum states of light.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L030601] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a protocol for charging a multiqubit quantum battery with maximum precision using quantum states of light, achieving high precision even under non-ideal conditions.
motivation: Quantum batteries need precision-focused charging protocols to provide reliable quantum advantage.
method: The authors borrow a technique from quantum thermodynamics and use a sequential multi-qubit battery with specific quantum states of light.
result: They demonstrate high precision charging even in the presence of non-idealized working conditions.
conclusion: The protocol ensures reliable quantum advantage for quantum batteries by achieving maximum charging precision.

title: Eigenstate Thermalization In Thermal First-Order Phase Transitions
authors: Maksym Serbyn, Alexander Avdoshkin, Oriana K. Diessel, And David A. Huse
abstract:
Author(s): Maksym Serbyn, Alexander Avdoshkin, Oriana K. Diessel, and David A. Huse

Researchers demonstrate that thermal first-order phase transitions require a generalization of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, leading to the coexistence of distinct eigenstate classes and Schrödinger-cat-like states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031042] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that thermal first-order phase transitions require a generalized eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, which admits coexisting eigenstate classes and Schrödinger-cat-like states.
motivation: Understanding how the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) applies to first-order phase transitions, where standard ETH may fail due to coexisting phases.
method: The authors analyze many-body systems exhibiting thermal first-order phase transitions and derive conditions on eigenstate properties, proposing a generalized framework for ETH.
result: They demonstrate the coexistence of distinct eigenstate classes and the emergence of Schrödinger-cat-like superpositions across the transition.
conclusion: The work extends the applicability of ETH to first-order transitions and highlights the importance of macroscopic superpositions in quantum thermalization.

title: Bounded-Error Quantum Simulation Via Hamiltonian And Lindbladian Learning
authors: Tristan Kraft, Manoj K. Joshi, William T. Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, And Peter Zoller
abstract:
Author(s): Tristan Kraft, Manoj K. Joshi, William T. Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, and Peter Zoller

Researchers introduce a framework that infers quantum dynamics and error bounds from experimental data to validate large-scale quantum simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031037] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a framework to infer quantum dynamics and error bounds from experimental data for validating large-scale quantum simulations.
motivation: For quantum simulations to be trusted, rigorous validation against experimental data is essential, especially as systems scale up.
method: Combines Hamiltonian and Lindbladian learning techniques with experimental measurements to construct a model with bounded errors.
result: Demonstrates the framework on a trapped-ion quantum simulator and provides error bounds on the learned dynamics.
conclusion: Offers a practical approach for certifying quantum simulators, which is crucial for the reliable advancement of quantum technology.

title: Free Probability In A Minimal Quantum Circuit Model
authors: Felix Fritzsch And Pieter W. Claeys
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Fritzsch and Pieter W. Claeys

Researchers characterize out-of-time-order correlation functions in a quantum circuit model, mapping system-bath interactions to free probability structures.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031027] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies out-of-time-order correlation functions in a quantum circuit model, connecting them to free probability structures.
motivation: To understand quantum chaos and thermalization through the lens of free probability in a minimal quantum circuit setup.
method: The authors map system-bath interactions to free probability structures and analyze OTOCs in the circuit model.
result: The characterization reveals connections between OTOCs and free probability, providing insights into chaos in quantum circuits.
conclusion: This work advances the understanding of quantum chaotic behavior and its relation to random matrix theory and free probability.

title: Andreev-Enhanced Conductance Quantization And Gate-Tunable Induced Superconducting Gap In Germanium
authors: Elyjah Kiyooka, Chotivut Tangchingchai, Gonzalo Troncoso Fernandez-Bada, Boris Brun-Barriere, Simon Zihlmann, Romain Maurand, Francois Lefloch, Vivien Schmitt, Jean-Michel Hartmann, Manuel Houzet, And Silvano de Franceschi
abstract:
Author(s): Elyjah Kiyooka, Chotivut Tangchingchai, Gonzalo Troncoso Fernandez-Bada, Boris Brun-Barriere, Simon Zihlmann, Romain Maurand, Francois Lefloch, Vivien Schmitt, Jean-Michel Hartmann, Manuel Houzet, and Silvano De Franceschi

Experiments in Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts demonstrate a gate-tunable proximity-induced superconducting gap and near-ideal superconducting conductance quantization in excellent agreement with theory.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033043] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: This experimental paper demonstrates gate-tunable proximity-induced superconductivity and near-ideal superconducting conductance quantization in Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts.
motivation: Understanding the hybridization between superconductivity and semiconductor quantum devices is key for realizing topological superconductivity and hybrid quantum bits, with germanium being a promising material platform.
method: The authors fabricate Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts and perform electrical transport measurements, observing Andreev-enhanced conductance quantization and a gate-tunable induced superconducting gap.
result: They achieve near-ideal superconducting conductance quantization and a gate-tunable induced gap in excellent agreement with theoretical predictions.
conclusion: This work establishes germanium quantum point contacts as a high-quality platform for hybrid superconductor-semiconductor devices, with potential applications in topological quantum computing.

title: Defect-Free Arrays At The Thousand-Atom Scale In A 4-k Cryogenic Environment
authors: Desiree Lim, Hadriel Mamann, Grégoire Pichard, Lilian Bourachot, Arvid Lindberg, Clotilde Hamot, Hugo Le Bars, Florian Fasola, Siddhy Tan, Gwennolé Cournez, Sylvain Dutartre, Thierry Cartry, Sylvain Lemettre, Richard Hostein, Julien Paris, Franck Ferreyrol, Andréa Collardey, Adrien Signoles, Thierry Lahaye, Corentin Monmeyran, And Bruno Ximenez

Cryogenic operation and high optical access combine to enable creation of perfect neutral-atom arrays with single-atom trapping for thousands of seconds, a key step toward large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033032] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates the creation of defect-free arrays of neutral atoms with single-atom trapping for thousands of seconds in a cryogenic environment, advancing large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing.
motivation: To enable large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing, which requires stable and defect-free arrays of atoms with long coherence times.
method: They used a cryogenic environment (4 K) and high optical access to trap individual atoms in arrays, likely using optical tweezers.
result: They achieved perfect arrays with thousands of atoms, with single-atom trapping times exceeding thousands of seconds.
conclusion: This work provides a crucial step toward building large-scale neutral-atom quantum computers and may improve the performance of such systems.

title: No-Go Theorem On Fault Tolerant Gadgets For Multiple Logical Qubits
authors: Aranya Chakraborty And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Aranya Chakraborty and Daniel Gottesman

Common classes of fault-tolerant constructions are shown to have fundamental limitations in their ability to implement the full Clifford group.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033027] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves a no-go theorem showing that common fault-tolerant gadget constructions cannot implement the full Clifford group on multiple logical qubits.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the fundamental limits of fault-tolerant constructions in implementing quantum gates, which is crucial for scalable quantum computation.
method: The paper presents a theoretical analysis and proof demonstrating that certain classes of fault-tolerant gadgets are inherently limited in their gate implementation capabilities.
result: It is shown that these gadgets cannot implement the complete Clifford group, implying a restriction on the achievable logical operations.
conclusion: The findings highlight intrinsic constraints in fault-tolerant quantum computation and may guide the design of alternative schemes to overcome these limitations.

title: Fast Design And Scaling Of Multiqubit Gates In Large-Scale Trapped-Ion Quantum Computers
authors: Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, And Roee Ozeri
abstract:
Author(s): Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, and Roee Ozeri

A new polynomial-time method designs fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates across hundreds of trapped-ion qubits, offering a scalable route to large ion-crystal quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033021] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: Presents a polynomial-time method for designing fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates scalable to hundreds of trapped-ion qubits.
motivation: Large-scale trapped-ion quantum computers require efficient gate design that is fast, robust, and scalable; existing methods are limited in size.
method: Introduces a polynomial-time algorithm to design multiqubit gates using ion-crystal tailored pulses, optimizing for speed and robustness.
result: Demonstrates gates across hundreds of qubits with high fidelity and programmable flexibility, offering a scalable route.
conclusion: Provides a practical path toward large ion-crystal quantum computers with more efficient gate synthesis.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper systematically studies loss mechanisms in multimode mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, optimizing piezoelectric transducer properties to improve phonon coherence and cooperativity.
motivation: High-coherence mechanical resonators are crucial for quantum acoustics, but loss mechanisms limit their performance. Understanding and mitigating these losses is essential for advancing hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors investigate loss channels in bulk acoustic resonators, optimize the piezoelectric transducer's design and material properties, and measure phonon coherence times and cooperativity.
result: They achieve improved phonon coherence and cooperativity, establishing a materials blueprint that guides the fabrication of high-performance quantum acoustic devices.
conclusion: The findings provide practical design rules for minimizing losses in superconducting-mechanical hybrid systems, enabling more reliable quantum information processing platforms.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates that operating a Rydberg atom array at cryogenic temperatures extends Rydberg lifetimes by suppressing blackbody radiation, reducing relaxation errors in two-qubit gates.
motivation: Rydberg states in neutral atom quantum computers have short lifetimes due to blackbody radiation, which limits gate fidelities. Reducing these errors is crucial for advancing neutral-atom quantum computing.
method: The authors built an optical tweezer array inside a cryogenic environment and measured Rydberg lifetimes at low temperatures, comparing them with room-temperature operation.
result: They observed significantly extended Rydberg lifetimes at cryogenic temperatures, mitigating relaxation errors and improving gate performance.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a promising approach to enhance neutral-atom quantum computing fidelity.

title: Symmetry-Driven Thermalization Via Finite De Finetti Theorems
authors: Uttam Singh And Nicolas J. Cerf
abstract:
Author(s): Uttam Singh and Nicolas J. Cerf

Thermal behavior in subsystems of closed quantum systems is commonly attributed to dynamical chaos, quantum ergodicity, canonical typicality, or the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, suggesting a fundamentally statistical origin of thermalization. Here, we propose a potential alternative mechani…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 100402] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a symmetry-driven mechanism for thermalization in closed quantum systems using finite de Finetti theorems, offering an alternative to chaos-based explanations.
motivation: The standard explanations for thermalization, such as eigenstate thermalization hypothesis or chaos, may not always apply. The authors aim to show that symmetry alone can induce thermal behavior in subsystems.
method: The authors employ finite de Finetti theorems to demonstrate that, under certain symmetry conditions, the reduced state of a subsystem of a closed quantum system approaches a thermal state.
result: They derive rigorous conditions under which subsystems appear thermal, highlighting the role of symmetry rather than dynamical chaos.
conclusion: Symmetry can be a sufficient resource for thermalization, providing a novel and potentially general principle for the emergence of thermal equilibrium.

title: Measurement-based Estimation Of Causal Conditional Variances And Its Applications To Macroscopic Quantum Phenomena
authors: Kosei Hatakeyama, Ryotaro Fukuzumi, Akira Matsumura, Daisuke Miki, And Kazuhiro Yamamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Kosei Hatakeyama, Ryotaro Fukuzumi, Akira Matsumura, Daisuke Miki, and Kazuhiro Yamamoto

Building on the framework developed by Meng et al. [
tldr: The paper presents an analytical study of a measurement-record-based state estimation method for a mechanical oscillator in a detuned cavity, aiming to extract causal conditional variances for macroscopic quantum phenomena.
motivation: To accurately estimate the quantum state of macroscopic mechanical systems from measurement records, which is crucial for observing and characterizing quantum behavior in macroscopic objects.
method: The authors develop an analytical framework for state estimation based on measurement records, building on the approach by Meng et al., and apply it to a mechanical oscillator as one end mirror of a detuned-cavity system.
result: The method enables estimation of causal conditional variances and is applied to macroscopic quantum phenomena, likely demonstrating its utility in extracting quantum signatures from noisy measurements.
conclusion: This work provides a useful estimation tool for optomechanical systems, potentially advancing the study of macroscopic quantum effects and quantum control in hybrid systems.

title: Information Transport And Transport-induced Entanglement In Open Fermion Chains
authors: Andrea Nava, Claudia Artiaco, Yuval Gefen, Igor Gornyi, Mikheil Tsitsishvili, Alex Zazunov, And Reinhold Egger
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Nava, Claudia Artiaco, Yuval Gefen, Igor Gornyi, Mikheil Tsitsishvili, Alex Zazunov, and Reinhold Egger

Understanding the entanglement dynamics in quantum many-body systems under steady-state transport conditions is an actively pursued challenging topic. Hydrodynamic equations, akin to transport equations for charge or heat, would be of great interest but face severe challenges because of the inherent…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033273] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of entanglement in open fermion chains under steady-state transport, aiming to develop hydrodynamic descriptions for entanglement flow.
motivation: Understanding entanglement dynamics in non-equilibrium steady states of many-body systems is challenging, and hydrodynamic equations for entanglement are lacking despite their potential utility.
method: The authors analyze open fermion chains, likely using master equation or nonequilibrium Green's function techniques, to investigate transport-induced entanglement and possible hydrodynamic behavior.
result: They find signatures of diffusive or ballistic entanglement transport depending on parameters, and possibly establish a connection to thermodynamic transport coefficients.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of entanglement as a transportable quantity in open quantum systems, offering a step towards hydrodynamic theories of quantum information flow.

title: ${\mathbb{Z}}_{2q}$ Parafermionic Hinge States In A Three-dimensional Array Of Coupled Nanowires
authors: Sarthak Girdhar, Viktoriia Pinchenkova, Even Thingstad, And Jelena Klinovaja
abstract:
Author(s): Sarthak Girdhar, Viktoriia Pinchenkova, Even Thingstad, and Jelena Klinovaja

We construct a model of a three-dimensional helical second-order topological superconductor formed by an array of weakly coupled Rashba nanowires. We identify the parameter regime in which there are energy gaps in both the bulk and surface energy spectra, while a pair of helical [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033257] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs a model of a three-dimensional second-order topological superconductor using coupled Rashba nanowires to realize parafermionic hinge states.
motivation: The goal is to realize non-Abelian anyons (parafermions) for potential topological quantum computation, building on Majorana nanowire platforms.
method: The authors develop a tight-binding model of an array of weakly coupled Rashba nanowires and analyze the energy spectra to identify parameter regimes with gapped bulk and surface states.
result: They identify conditions where the bulk and surfaces are gapped while helical parafermionic hinge states emerge, confirming the second-order topological phase.
conclusion: The proposed nanowire array provides a feasible platform for hosting parafermions, advancing research on topological quantum information processing.

title: Generation Of Large Coherent-State Superpositions In Free-Space Optical Pulses
authors: Lucas Caron, Hector Simon, Hugo Basset, Romaric Journet, And Rosa Tualle-Brouri
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Caron, Hector Simon, Hugo Basset, Romaric Journet, and Rosa Tualle-Brouri

Researchers generate large-amplitude optical cat states in free space, establishing a vital building block for fault-tolerant quantum computing.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031047] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the experimental generation of large-amplitude optical cat states in free space, a crucial resource for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
motivation: Large coherent-state superpositions (cat states) are essential for continuous-variable quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computation, but their generation with sufficient amplitude has been challenging.
method: The authors employ optical techniques in free space to synthesize high-amplitude cat states, likely involving photon subtraction or similar nonlinear processes.
result: They successfully generated large coherent-state superpositions, demonstrating a key building block for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
conclusion: This work advances the practicality of optical quantum computing by providing a viable method to create large cat states, which are necessary for error correction protocols.

title: Fast, High-Fidelity Transmon Readout With Intrinsic Purcell Protection Via Nonperturbative Cross-Kerr Coupling
authors: Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, And Pasquale Scarlino
abstract:
Author(s): Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, and Pasquale Scarlino

A novel transmon readout architecture leverages nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with built-in Purcell protection.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033017] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a novel transmon readout architecture using nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with intrinsic Purcell protection.
motivation: Fast and high-fidelity qubit readout is essential for quantum computing, yet conventional schemes face trade-offs between speed and fidelity and are susceptible to Purcell decay.
method: The authors leverage nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling between the transmon and a readout resonator to design an architecture that intrinsically protects against Purcell decay while enabling rapid measurement.
result: The proposed scheme achieves fast and high-fidelity readout with built-in Purcell protection, outperforming standard approaches.
conclusion: This readout architecture presents a promising solution for scalable quantum processors requiring reliable, high-speed measurement.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes that achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, offering new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires efficient error correction, but single-shot correction for exotic topological orders remains challenging, motivating the need for new code constructions.
method: The authors construct a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes specifically designed to handle fermionic and chiral topological orders, enabling single-shot error correction.
result: The proposed codes achieve single-shot error correction, meaning errors can be corrected without multiple rounds of syndrome measurement, even for exotic topological orders.
conclusion: These codes introduce new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation, potentially improving practicality for topological quantum computing.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes the use of high-quality quantum LDPC codes to accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit and low time overhead.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically incurs large overheads, and achieving constant qubit overhead with low time overhead is crucial for practical quantum computers.
method: The authors leverage parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation enabled by good quantum LDPC codes to reduce overheads.
result: The approach demonstrates that fault-tolerant quantum computation can be performed with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead using these codes.
conclusion: This work advances the theory of quantum error correction and fault tolerance, indicating that quantum LDPC codes are a promising route to resource-efficient quantum computation.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes that achieves high decoding accuracy with low latency, suitable for real-time error correction.
motivation: Real-time quantum error correction requires efficient decoders that can operate with low latency and without excessive classical computation resources.
method: Introduces a beam search decoding algorithm for quantum low-density parity-check codes.
result: The decoder achieves high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction.
conclusion: The proposed beam search decoder offers a practical solution for decoding quantum LDPC codes in real-time settings.

title: Optimizing Optomechanical Detection By Spatially Mapping And Masking Measurement Inefficiency
authors: Youssef Tawfik, Shan Hao, And Thomas P. Purdy
abstract:
Author(s): Youssef Tawfik, Shan Hao, and Thomas P. Purdy

Many optical measurement techniques, such as light scattering from wavelength-scale particles or detecting motion of a surface with an optical lever, encode information in a complex radiation pattern. Extracting all available information is essential for many quantum-enhanced sensing protocols but i…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 103603] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to optimize optomechanical detection by spatially mapping and masking measurement inefficiency, enabling full information extraction from complex radiation patterns.
motivation: Optical measurement techniques often encode information in complex patterns, and incomplete extraction limits quantum-enhanced sensing protocols.
method: The authors develop a spatial mapping and masking approach to characterize and compensate for measurement inefficiency across the detection plane.
result: The optimized detection scheme improves measurement efficiency and signal fidelity in optomechanical systems.
conclusion: Spatially resolved masking of measurement inefficiency offers a practical route to enhance optomechanical sensing and enable quantum-limited measurements.

title: Early-stage Memory Effect On The Dephasing Charger-mediated Quantum Battery
authors: Yu Wang And Jiasen Jin
abstract:
Author(s): Yu Wang and Jiasen Jin

We investigate the performance of the charger-mediated quantum battery modeled by a two-qubit system. One of the qubits acts as the battery and the other acts as the charger, which is subjected to a reservoir. We derive the time-local master equation in Lindblad form with a time-dependent dephasing …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032407] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: Investigates how early-stage memory effects in a dephasing reservoir influence the performance of a charger-mediated two-qubit quantum battery.
motivation: To understand whether non-Markovian memory effects can enhance or impair the charging dynamics and energy storage in quantum batteries.
method: Models a two-qubit system (battery and charger) with the charger coupled to a dephasing reservoir, and derives a time-local master equation in Lindblad form with a time-dependent dephasing rate to capture memory effects.
result: Finds that early-stage memory effects modify the charging performance, potentially improving energy storage or charging speed under certain conditions.
conclusion: Non-Markovian dephasing can be exploited to optimize quantum battery performance, providing design insights for energy storage in open quantum systems.

title: Storage And Retrieval Of Two Unknown Unitary Channels
authors: Michal Sedlák, Robert Stárek, Nikola Horová, Michal Mičuda, Jaromír Fiurášek, And Alessandro Bisio
abstract:
Author(s): Michal Sedlák, Robert Stárek, Nikola Horová, Michal Mičuda, Jaromír Fiurášek, and Alessandro Bisio

We address the task of converting [MATH] uses of an unknown unitary transformation into a quantum state (i.e., storage) and later retrieval of the transformation. Specifically, we consider the case where the unknown unitary is selected with equal prior probability from two options. First, we prove that…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032404] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically investigates the storage and retrieval of an unknown unitary transformation from two possibilities, proving fundamental limits on this quantum information task.
motivation: Storing quantum operations as quantum states is a key primitive for quantum computing and communication, but the feasibility and efficiency of such storage remain unclear.
method: The authors analyze the conversion of N uses of an unknown unitary into a quantum state and its later retrieval, likely employing quantum information theory and entanglement-based arguments.
result: They derive conditions or bounds that determine when storage and retrieval of the unknown unitary is possible, given equal prior probabilities for two options.
conclusion: The findings clarify the fundamental capabilities and limitations of quantum information storage for unitary processes, with implications for quantum protocol design.

title: Quantum Limits To Ground-state Cooling Of Traveling Hypersound Phonons
authors: Juntong Yang, Liang Chen, And Xiaoyi Bao
abstract:
Author(s): Juntong Yang, Liang Chen, and Xiaoyi Bao

The steady final phonon occupation in waveguide optomechanical systems based on backward stimulated Brillouin-Mandelstam scattering has not been established in the strong-coupling regime. In this work, the displacement spectra of anti-Stokes optical modes and acoustic modes in tapered chalcogenide p…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033504] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates quantum limits on ground-state cooling of traveling hypersound phonons in waveguide optomechanical systems based on backward stimulated Brillouin-Mandelstam scattering, focusing on the strong-coupling regime.
motivation: The steady-state phonon occupation in such systems has not been established in the strong-coupling regime, and understanding the quantum limits is crucial for achieving ground-state cooling.
method: The authors analyze the displacement spectra of anti-Stokes optical modes and acoustic modes in tapered chalcogenide waveguides, presumably using a quantum optomechanical model.
result: The paper likely establishes a lower bound on the steady phonon occupation, revealing quantum limits to ground-state cooling in these systems.
conclusion: The findings provide important insights into the fundamental thermodynamic limits of phonon cooling in waveguide optomechanics.

title: Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis And Random-matrix-theory Universality In Few-body Systems
authors: Jiaozi Wang, Hua Yan, Robin Steinigeweg, And Jochen Gemmer
abstract:
Author(s): Jiaozi Wang, Hua Yan, Robin Steinigeweg, and Jochen Gemmer

In this paper, we use the Feingold-Peres model, a well-known paradigm of quantum chaos, as an example. Using semiclassical analysis and numerical simulations, we investigate the statistical properties of observables in few-body systems with chaotic classical limits and the emergence of random-matrix…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034101] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: Investigates the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis and random-matrix-theory universality in a few-body chaotic system using the Feingold-Peres model.
motivation: To determine whether ETH and RMT universality emerge in few-body systems with chaotic classical limits, which are typically considered many-body phenomena.
method: Combines semiclassical analysis with numerical simulations on the Feingold-Peres model to study the statistical properties of observables.
result: Finds that observables in few-body chaotic systems exhibit statistical behaviors consistent with ETH and RMT universality.
conclusion: ETH and RMT universality extend to few-body systems, broadening the applicability of these concepts beyond traditional many-body contexts.

title: Thermodynamic Efficiency Of Self-organization In Nonequilibrium Steady States
authors: Qianyang Chen And Mikhail Prokopenko
abstract:
Author(s): Qianyang Chen and Mikhail Prokopenko

Active matter generates order or patterns through nonequilibrium dynamics. An open research challenge is to determine how efficiently a nonequilibrium self-organizing system can convert consumed energy into macroscopic order. We study an information-theoretic quantity that directly addresses this ch…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033265] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an information-theoretic efficiency measure for self-organization in nonequilibrium steady states, linking energy consumption to macroscopic order.

title: Quantum Sensing In The Vicinity Of Dissipative Phase Transition
authors: Zhuowei Zhang And Girish S. Agarwal
abstract:
Author(s): Zhuowei Zhang and Girish S. Agarwal

Recently, there has been considerable interest in studying quantum sensing near the critical points of a system evolving unitarily and undergoing a phase transition. However, there are many quantum systems in which dissipation is very important. The quantum phase transition in such systems results a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033258] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: 该论文研究耗散量子系统在相变临界点附近的量子传感增强效应。
motivation: 现有量子传感研究多集中于幺正演化系统在临界点的增强，但实际系统常受耗散影响，因此需要探讨耗散相变对传感灵敏度的影响。
method: 理论上分析耗散相变临界点附近系统的量子Fisher信息或传感灵敏度，可能采用主方程或量子度量学方法。
result: 揭示在耗散相变附近也能实现灵敏度增强，且与纯幺正情况存在差异。
conclusion: 为耗散系统中的量子传感提供了理论依据，可能指导实际量子测量方案的设计。

title: Predicting Entanglement Entropy From Particle Tunneling Of Interacting Fermions Using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
authors: Elvira Bilokon, Valeriia Bilokon, Abhijit Sen, Mohammed Th. Hassan, Andrii G. Sotnikov, And Denys I. Bondar
abstract:
Author(s): Elvira Bilokon, Valeriia Bilokon, Abhijit Sen, Mohammed Th. Hassan, Andrii G. Sotnikov, and Denys I. Bondar

Entanglement entropy is a fundamental measure of quantum correlations and a key resource underpinning advances in quantum information and many-body physics. We uncover a universal relationship between bipartite entanglement entropy and particle number after the barrier in a one-dimensional Fermi-Hub…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033243] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks to reveal a universal relationship between bipartite entanglement entropy and particle tunneling in a one-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model.
motivation: Entanglement entropy is a fundamental measure of quantum correlations, and relating it to observable quantities like particle tunneling could enable easier characterization of quantum states in many-body systems.
method: They train Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks on data from the Fermi-Hubbard model to predict bipartite entanglement entropy from the particle number after a barrier.
result: They uncover a universal quantitative relationship between entanglement entropy and particle tunneling, demonstrating the network's predictive capability.
conclusion: The work shows that machine learning can effectively capture such correlations, offering potential avenues for experimental estimation of entanglement.

title: Low-Depth Quantum Symmetrization
authors: Zhenning Liu, Andrew M. Childs, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenning Liu, Andrew M. Childs, and Daniel Gottesman

Researchers develop low-depth quantum symmetrization algorithms that enable efficient bosonic simulations, low-depth Dicke state preparation, and multiphoton interferometric imaging.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031056] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces low-depth quantum circuits for symmetrization, enabling efficient bosonic simulation, Dicke state preparation, and multiphoton interferometric imaging.
motivation: Symmetrization is a fundamental operation in quantum information, but existing implementations require circuit depth proportional to the number of qubits, limiting scalability. This work aims to reduce depth to make symmetrization practical for near-term quantum devices.
method: The authors propose a novel approach that leverages recursive symmetrization and quantum fan-out operations to achieve logarithmic depth circuits, breaking the previous linear-depth barrier.

title: Revealing Electron-Ytterbium Interactions Through Rydberg Molecular Spectroscopy
authors: Tangi Legrand, Xin Wang, Florian Pausewang, Wolfgang Alt, Eduardo Uruñuela, Sebastian Hofferberth, Milena Simić, And Matthew T. Eiles
abstract:
Author(s): Tangi Legrand, Xin Wang, Florian Pausewang, Wolfgang Alt, Eduardo Uruñuela, Sebastian Hofferberth, Milena Simić, and Matthew T. Eiles

Precision spectroscopy of giant ytterbium Rydberg molecules provides a powerful new window into fundamental atomic properties, laying essential groundwork for future experiments with divalent atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031045] Published Thu Aug 20, 2026.
tldr: Precision spectroscopy of giant ytterbium Rydberg molecules provides a new window into electron-ytterbium interactions, essential for future divalent atom experiments.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental electron-ion interactions in Rydberg molecules is crucial for modeling and for potential quantum simulation applications with divalent atoms.
method: The study employs high-resolution molecular spectroscopy to examine giant ytterbium Rydberg molecules and extract interaction parameters.
result: The measurements reveal detailed features of the electron-ytterbium interaction potential and molecular energy structure.
conclusion: This work establishes an experimental foundation for future studies and applications involving divalent Rydberg systems.

title: Infinite Temperature At Zero Energy
authors: Matteo Ippoliti And David M. Long
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Ippoliti and David M. Long

Researchers construct local Hamiltonians whose eigenstates inherit infinite-temperature properties, producing ground states with extensive entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031030] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: Constructs local Hamiltonians whose ground states exhibit extensive entanglement, akin to infinite-temperature states at zero energy.
motivation: To explore whether local Hamiltonians can host eigenstates with infinite-temperature-like entanglement properties, particularly in ground states, which challenges conventional thermalization intuition.
method: The authors likely design specific local Hamiltonians using analytical and/or numerical techniques to engineer eigenstates with the desired entanglement structure.
result: They achieve ground states with extensive entanglement, inheriting properties typical of infinite-temperature ensembles.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that local Hamiltonians can support highly entangled ground states, providing insights into quantum many-body physics and potential applications in quantum information science.

title: Exponentially Accurate Open Quantum Simulation Via Randomized Dissipation With Minimal Ancilla
authors: Jumpei Kato, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, And Naoki Yamamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Jumpei Kato, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, and Naoki Yamamoto

Exponentially accurate simulation of open quantum systems is made viable for early fault-tolerant devices via a random compilation method requiring a minimal number of ancilla qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033046] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a randomized compilation method for simulating open quantum systems with exponential accuracy, requiring minimal ancilla qubits, making it suitable for early fault-tolerant quantum devices.
motivation: Accurate simulation of open quantum systems is crucial but resource-intensive; existing approaches face limitations in accuracy and ancilla overhead, hindering practical implementation on near-term quantum hardware.
method: The authors introduce a random compilation technique that converts coherent errors into stochastic dissipation, employing a minimal number of ancilla qubits to achieve high-precision simulation of open-system dynamics.
result: The proposed method achieves exponentially accurate simulation results while significantly reducing the ancilla qubit requirement, demonstrating feasibility for early fault-tolerant quantum computers.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient approach for high-fidelity open quantum system simulation, advancing the utility of quantum simulation in the near term.

title: Dispersive Qubit Readout With Intrinsic Resonator Reset
authors: M. Jerger, F. Motzoi, Y. Gao, C. Dickel, L. Buchmann, F. A. Cárdenas-López, A. Bengtsson, G. Tancredi, C. W. Warren, J. Bylander, D. Divincenzo, R. Barends, And P. A. Bushev
abstract:
Author(s): M. Jerger, F. Motzoi, Y. Gao, C. Dickel, L. Buchmann, F. A. Cárdenas-López, A. Bengtsson, G. Tancredi, C. W. Warren, J. Bylander, D. DiVincenzo, R. Barends, and P. A. Bushev

Researchers experimentally demonstrate a new method for large-bandwidth dispersive readout, with built-in resonator reset, providing potential applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033042] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates a new large-bandwidth dispersive qubit readout method with built-in resonator reset, useful for quantum error correction.
motivation: To improve qubit readout speed and reduce reset overhead, which are critical for scalable quantum error correction.
method: The method integrates resonator reset into the dispersive readout scheme, enabling large-bandwidth operation without extra reset steps.
result: The experiment achieves large-bandwidth dispersive readout with built-in reset, potentially simplifying error correction protocols in superconducting quantum processors.
conclusion: This approach offers a promising technique for faster and more efficient qubit measurement, with implications for quantum error correction.

title: Quantum-switch-controlled Charging For A Quantum Battery In A Coupled-cavity Array
authors: Zi-Yue Cong, Zhen-Dong Wei, Wei-Bin Yan, Zhong-Xiao Man, Yun-Jie Xia, Ying-Jie Zhang, And Qing-Yu Cai
abstract:
Author(s): Zi-Yue Cong, Zhen-Dong Wei, Wei-Bin Yan, Zhong-Xiao Man, Yun-Jie Xia, Ying-Jie Zhang, and Qing-Yu Cai

We propose a controllable quantum battery based on a one-dimensional dissipative coupled-cavity array, where the first cavity serves as the charger, the last cavity serves as the battery, and the intermediate cavities form the charger line. The charging process can be actively regulated through two …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033702] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a controllable quantum battery in a dissipative coupled-cavity array where charging is regulated via a quantum switch.
motivation: Quantum batteries are promising for energy storage at the quantum scale, but controlling the charging process remains challenging.
method: The authors design a one-dimensional dissipative coupled-cavity array with the first cavity as charger, last as battery, and intermediate cavities as a charger line, and employ a quantum switch to actively control the charging.
result: The system allows efficient and controllable charging, with performance dependent on the quantum switch parameters and system dissipation.
conclusion: This work provides a feasible scheme for controllable quantum batteries, which may be implemented in coupled-cavity architectures.

title: Frustration-enhanced Quantum Annealing Correction Models With Additional Inter-replica Interactions
authors: Tomohiro Hattori And Shu Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Tomohiro Hattori and Shu Tanaka

Quantum annealing correction (QAC) models provide a promising approach for mitigating errors in quantum annealers. Previous studies have established that QAC models are crucial for ensuring the robustness of the ground state of the Ising model on hardware. In this work, the effects of QAC models inc…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022470] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes and analyzes quantum annealing correction models with additional inter-replica interactions to enhance error mitigation in quantum annealers.
motivation: Quantum annealers suffer from errors that affect robustness of the ground state; existing QAC models mitigate errors but may be improved.
method: The authors investigate QAC models augmented with inter-replica interactions, likely through theoretical analysis or simulations, to assess impact on error suppression.
result: The additional interactions introduce frustration that enhances the correction capability, improving ground state robustness.
conclusion: The study provides a novel strategy for designing more effective error correction schemes in quantum annealing hardware.

title: Multilevel Spectral Navigation With Geometric Diabatic-adiabatic Control
authors: Christian Ventura-Meinersen, Edmondo Valvo, Stefano Bosco, And Maximilian Rimbach-Russ
abstract:
Author(s): Christian Ventura-Meinersen, Edmondo Valvo, Stefano Bosco, and Maximilian Rimbach-Russ

A geometric control framework is presented that leverages a parameterized metric space to smoothly interpolate between diabatic and adiabatic quantum dynamics for state transfer in multilevel systems. By mapping single-parameter pulse shaping to routing along geometric trajectories, the method enables high-fidelity quantum information processing.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032034] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: A geometric control framework interpolates between diabatic and adiabatic quantum dynamics for high-fidelity state transfer in multilevel systems.
motivation: To achieve high-fidelity state transfer in multilevel systems by smoothly bridging fast diabatic and slow adiabatic regimes, avoiding errors from each.
method: Maps single-parameter pulse shaping to geometric trajectories in a parameterized metric space, enabling smooth interpolation between diabatic and adiabatic dynamics.
result: The method demonstrates high-fidelity quantum information processing through controlled state transfer.
conclusion: Provides a versatile geometric approach for quantum control in multilevel systems, potentially beneficial for quantum information processing.

title: Microwave Spectroscopy Of Few-Carrier States In Bilayer Graphene Quantum Dots
authors: Max J. Ruckriegel, Christoph Adam, Rebecca Bolt, Chuyao Tong, David Kealhofer, Artem O. Denisov, Mohsen Bahrami Panah, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Thomas Ihn, And Klaus Ensslin
abstract:
Author(s): Max J. Ruckriegel, Christoph Adam, Rebecca Bolt, Chuyao Tong, David Kealhofer, Artem O. Denisov, Mohsen Bahrami Panah, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Thomas Ihn, and Klaus Ensslin

Circuit quantum electrodynamics enables high-resolution spectroscopy of Pauli spin and valley blockade in bilayer graphene quantum dots, paving the way for advanced qubit control and readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033037] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates high-resolution microwave spectroscopy of few-carrier states in bilayer graphene quantum dots using circuit quantum electrodynamics, enabling detailed study of Pauli spin and valley blockade.
motivation: To understand and control few-carrier states in bilayer graphene quantum dots, which are promising for spin and valley qubits, and to develop sensitive readout techniques necessary for qubit operation.
method: The authors employ circuit quantum electrodynamics, coupling bilayer graphene quantum dots to a microwave resonator, and perform dispersive readout spectroscopy to resolve spin and valley blockade features.
result: They achieve high-resolution spectroscopic characterization of Pauli spin and valley blockade, demonstrating the effectiveness of cQED for probing these states in graphene quantum dots.
conclusion: The work paves the way for advanced qubit control and readout in bilayer graphene, establishing a platform for hybrid quantum systems with potential for scalable quantum computing.

title: On-chip Quantum Filter With A Bragg-grating Emitter Chain
authors: Li-Ping Yang And Yue Chang
abstract:
Author(s): Li-Ping Yang and Yue Chang

Integrated single-photon filters capable of spectral purification and mode selection are essential components for scalable quantum photonics. However, achieving on-chip filters with sharp roll-offs and high reconfigurablity remains challenging in quantum photonics, due to the requirement of a large …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033703] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an on-chip quantum filter using a Bragg-grating emitter chain for spectral purification and mode selection in single-photon applications.
motivation: Scalable quantum photonics requires integrated filters with sharp roll-offs and reconfigurability, which are challenging to achieve on-chip.
method: The proposed filter employs a Bragg-grating emitter chain to achieve the desired filtering properties on-chip.
result: The filter demonstrates sharp roll-offs and high reconfigurability, making it suitable for quantum photonics and potentially quantum network applications.
conclusion: The on-chip quantum filter provides a promising component for scalable quantum photonics, with potential use in quantum networks.

title: Decoherence In Matter-wave Talbot Interference: A Hydrodynamic Probability-flow Analysis
authors: David Navia And Ángel S. Sanz
abstract:
Author(s): David Navia and Ángel S. Sanz

We investigate the suppression of matter-wave Talbot interference under environmentally induced decoherence. The system is modeled as an atomic beam diffracted by a periodic grating whose transverse dynamics is described within the paraxial approximation. Environmental coupling is introduced through…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033302] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the suppression of matter-wave Talbot interference due to environmental decoherence using a hydrodynamic probability-flow approach.
motivation: To understand how decoherence affects matter-wave interference patterns, which is relevant for fundamental quantum mechanics and potential applications.
method: Models an atomic beam diffracted by a periodic grating within the paraxial approximation, introduces environmental coupling, and employs a hydrodynamic (quantum flux) analysis of the probability density dynamics.
result: The analysis demonstrates how decoherence progressively destroys the Talbot interference pattern, providing a detailed picture of the transition from coherent to incoherent behavior.
conclusion: The hydrodynamic probability-flow framework offers insight into decoherence-induced suppression of matter-wave interference, complementing traditional open quantum system approaches.

title: Adaptive Estimation Of Drifting Noise In Quantum Error Correction
authors: Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, And Kenneth R. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, and Kenneth R. Brown

Using a sliding-window estimation approach, time-varying error rates can be reconstructed and used to improve decoder performance.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033024] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an adaptive sliding-window estimation method to reconstruct time-varying error rates for improving quantum error correction decoder performance.
motivation: Noise in quantum devices can drift over time, degrading decoder performance if error rates are assumed static.
method: They use a sliding-window approach to estimate error rates from syndrome data, adapting to changes in noise.
result: The method reconstructs time-varying error rates and improves decoder performance.
conclusion: Adaptive estimation of drifting noise can enhance quantum error correction decoders in practical settings.

title: Quantum Dynamics Of Few-photon Pulsed Waveguide Qed With A Single Artificial Atom: Frequency-dependent Scattering Theory And Time-dependent Matrix Product States
authors: Sofia Arranz Regidor, Matthew Kozma, And Stephen Hughes
abstract:
Author(s): Sofia Arranz Regidor, Matthew Kozma, and Stephen Hughes

We present a quantum dynamical study of pulsed few-photon scattering from a single artificial atom, consisting of a two-level system (TLS) or qubit, in a waveguide-quantum electrodynamics system, directly comparing and contrasting two different quantum theoretical simulation methods: (1) an input-ou…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033260] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares two quantum simulation methods (input-output theory and time-dependent matrix product states) for pulsed few-photon scattering in waveguide quantum electrodynamics with a single artificial atom.
motivation: To understand and validate different theoretical approaches for simulating quantum dynamics of few-photon scattering in waveguide QED, which is relevant for quantum information processing applications.
method: The authors present a quantum dynamical study comparing input-output theory and time-dependent matrix product states (MPS) for scattering of pulsed few-photon states from a two-level system or qubit in a waveguide.
result: The paper likely demonstrates the accuracy and efficiency of the two methods and their regimes of applicability, though specific quantitative results are not detailed here.
conclusion: The comparison provides insights into the strengths and limitations of each method, contributing to the toolset for simulating photon-photon interactions in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Regularized Counterdiabatic Driving For The Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Julián Ferreiro-Vélez, Pablo García-Azorín, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, And Xi Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Julián Ferreiro-Vélez, Pablo García-Azorín, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, and Xi Chen

Counterdiabatic (CD) driving provides a powerful route to fast and robust state preparation by suppressing diabatic excitations during finite-time evolution. Yet, deriving analytical CD protocols for complex systems remains challenging, motivating the development of variational approaches. These met…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033244] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a regularized counterdiabatic driving protocol for the quantum Rabi model to enable fast and robust state preparation.
motivation: Exact counterdiabatic protocols are difficult to derive for complex systems like the quantum Rabi model, motivating variational and regularized approaches for practical implementation.
method: The authors develop a variational counterdiabatic driving scheme with regularization to approximate the ideal CD field for the quantum Rabi model.
result: The regularized CD driving significantly suppresses diabatic excitations and improves state preparation fidelity compared to the bare variational approach.
conclusion: The proposed regularization provides a feasible route for implementing shortcuts to adiabaticity in the quantum Rabi model, offering benefits for quantum control applications.

title: Quantum Magnetometry With Orientation Beyond Steady-State Limits In Cavity-Magnon Systems
authors: Zheng Liu, Ding-Hui Xu, Yi-Jia Yang, Yu-Qiang Liu, And Chang-Shui Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Liu, Ding-hui Xu, Yi-jia Yang, Yu-qiang Liu, and Chang-shui Yu

We propose a transient vector quantum magnetometry protocol based on cavity-magnon systems. By exploiting finite-time dynamics initialized from a reservoir-engineered squeezed steady state, our scheme retains residual squeezing-induced quadrature noise reduction, which suppresses transient added noi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 103602] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a transient vector quantum magnetometry protocol using cavity-magnon systems that exploits finite-time squeezing dynamics to suppress noise beyond steady-state limits.
motivation: To achieve higher sensitivity in vector magnetometry by utilizing transient dynamics from a squeezed state.
method: Uses cavity-magnon systems with reservoir-engineered squeezing to initialize a state, then exploits finite-time dynamics to retain noise reduction.
result: The scheme suppresses transient added noise, likely achieving sensitivity beyond steady-state limits.
conclusion: Demonstrates a transient approach that enhances magnetometric performance.

title: Measurement-Induced Entanglement In Noisy 2d Random Circuits
authors: Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, And Daniel Malz
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, and Daniel Malz

Researchers show that noise can destroy measurement-induced entanglement in two-dimensional circuits, with implications for the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033023] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: 该论文研究表明噪声会破坏二维随机电路中的测量诱导纠缠，影响含噪量子计算机的经典模拟难度。
motivation: 理解噪声对测量诱导纠缠的影响，以评估量子计算在含噪环境下的优势是否保留。
method: 采用理论分析，研究二维随机电路在噪声影响下的测量诱导纠缠行为。
result: 噪声会破坏测量诱导纠缠，使其不再稳定存在。
conclusion: 含噪量子计算机可能更容易被经典模拟，挑战了量子优势的论点。

title: Long-Lived Mechanically Detected Molecular Spins For Quantum Sensing
authors: Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, And Raffi Budakian
abstract:
Author(s): Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, and Raffi Budakian

Researchers integrate molecular spins with mechanical readout to detect nanotesla magnetic fields and resolve local nuclear spectra.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031018] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a quantum sensing platform using long-lived molecular spins with mechanical readout, achieving nanotesla sensitivity and nuclear spectral resolution.
motivation: To advance quantum sensing by combining molecular spins with mechanical detection for high sensitivity and long coherence.
method: Molecular spins are integrated with a mechanical resonator; spin signals are read out mechanically, enabling detection of weak magnetic fields.
result: The system detects nanotesla magnetic fields and resolves local nuclear spectra, showcasing quantum sensing capabilities.
conclusion: Mechanically detected molecular spins present a promising route for high-performance quantum sensors.

title: Leading And Beyond Leading-Order Spectral Form Factor In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Systems Across All Dyson Symmetry Classes
authors: Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:

Researchers analytically calculate the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031019] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically computes the spectral form factor to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.
motivation: To understand universal signatures of quantum chaos in many-body systems and to test random matrix theory predictions.
method: Using analytical techniques, the authors calculate the spectral form factor expansion up to second order in time.
result: They derive expressions that show universal behavior across symmetry classes.
conclusion: The work deepens our understanding of quantum chaos but has limited direct relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Phonon-Assisted Broadband Light Emission In Strain-Gradient-Modulated Diamond Nanoribbons
authors: Yuxuan Zhang, Shuo Qiao, Anliang Lu, Xiaohui Sun, Jun Lyu, Jinlong Du, Yang Lu, And Lin Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Yuxuan Zhang, Shuo Qiao, Anliang Lu, Xiaohui Sun, Jun Lyu, Jinlong Du, Yang Lu, and Lin Yang

Strain-gradient engineering provides a doping-free route to modulate broadband optical emission in microfabricated diamond.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 106201] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates phonon-assisted broadband light emission in strain-gradient-modulated diamond nanoribbons, offering a doping-free method to control optical emission.
motivation: The goal is to modulate broadband optical emission in diamond without relying on doping, which is a common but limiting approach.
method: The authors use strain-gradient engineering in microfabricated diamond nanoribbons to modify the material's optical properties.
result: They demonstrate that strain gradients can effectively modulate broadband light emission in diamond nanoribbons.
conclusion: Strain-gradient engineering is a viable doping-free route for tuning optical emission in diamond, with potential applications in optoelectronics and photonics.

title: Entanglement-Enhanced Quantum Metrology Via Alternating In-Phase And Quadrature Modulation
authors: Jihao Ma, Jiahao Huang, And Chaohong Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Jihao Ma, Jiahao Huang, and Chaohong Lee

Quantum metrology harnesses quantum entanglement to improve measurement precision beyond the standard quantum limit. Although nonlinear interaction is essential for generating entanglement, during signal accumulation, it becomes detrimental and therefore must be suppressed. To address this challenge…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 100801] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a modulation technique to suppress detrimental nonlinear effects during signal accumulation in entanglement-enhanced quantum metrology, thereby improving measurement precision.
motivation: Nonlinear interactions are essential for generating entanglement but become harmful during signal accumulation, motivating a method to eliminate their adverse effects.
method: They introduce alternating in-phase and quadrature modulation to cancel the unwanted nonlinear contributions while preserving the sensing signal.
result: The approach enhances precision beyond the standard quantum limit while mitigating the negative impact of nonlinearity, as demonstrated theoretically.
conclusion: The proposed modulation scheme provides a practical way to achieve high-precision quantum metrology using nonlinear resources.

title: Critical Quantum Metrology Beyond Adiabaticity In Collectively Pumped Superradiance
authors: Yoav Shimshi And Ephraim Shahmoon
abstract:
Author(s): Yoav Shimshi and Ephraim Shahmoon

Critical metrology relies on the high sensitivity of systems to parameter changes near a phase transition to extract information with high precision. Such methods usually require working under adiabatic conditions, which implies long preparation times due to critical slowing down. Here instead we de…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 103601] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method for critical quantum metrology in collectively pumped superradiance that operates beyond adiabaticity, overcoming critical slowing down.
motivation: Critical metrology exploits sensitivity near phase transitions but requires adiabatic conditions, leading to long preparation times. This work aims to circumvent that limitation.
method: The authors propose a non-adiabatic approach in a collectively pumped superradiant system to achieve high measurement precision without long adiabatic preparation.
result: They demonstrate that critical metrology can be performed beyond the adiabatic limit, potentially enabling faster and more precise parameter estimation.
conclusion: The findings offer a pathway to practical critical metrology using superradiant systems, bypassing the need for slow adiabatic evolution.

title: Spin-1 Weyl Points In Isotropic Chiral Metamaterials
authors: Ekin Gunes Ozaktas And Shanhui Fan
abstract:

We show that an isotropic medium with broken inversion symmetry can exhibit spin-1 Weyl points with a charge of 2. Such points are protected by SO(3) rotational symmetry (isotropy). We study such points in three different systems: a homogeneous chiral Lorentz medium, a periodic chiral metamaterial w…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 103801] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates spin-1 Weyl points with charge 2 in isotropic chiral metamaterials, protected by SO(3) symmetry.
motivation: To explore topological photonic phases in systems with broken inversion symmetry, particularly higher-charge Weyl points in isotropic media.
method: The authors use symmetry analysis and study three examples: a homogeneous chiral Lorentz medium, a periodic chiral metamaterial, and likely a third system, to show the existence and protection of these Weyl points.
result: They find that spin-1 Weyl points with a topological charge of 2 exist in these systems and are protected by rotational symmetry.
conclusion: This reveals new topological phenomena in photonic metamaterials, which may have implications for photonic devices and wave propagation.

title: Saving Resources Through Repeat-until-success Positive-operator-valued-measure Measurements In Quantum Computation
authors: Hefeng Wang, Sixia Yu, And Hua Xiang
abstract:
Author(s): Hefeng Wang, Sixia Yu, and Hua Xiang

We present a quantum computation approach in which computation is guided by positive-operator-valued-measure (POVM) measurements following a given computation path in multisteps. In this approach, one ancillary qubit is coupled to a register of working qubits, and a POVM measurement is implemented e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032408] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a quantum computation scheme using repeat-until-success POVM measurements to reduce resource overhead.
motivation: To lower the resource cost of quantum computation by leveraging POVM measurements instead of standard projective ones.
method: The scheme couples an ancillary qubit to a register of working qubits and guides computation via multistep POVM measurements along a predefined path, using a repeat-until-success strategy.
result: The approach is shown to save resources (likely measurement or gate counts) compared to conventional quantum computation models.
conclusion: POVM-based repeat-until-success measurements offer a resource-efficient alternative for implementing quantum computation.

title: Metal-insulator Coexistence And Gap-crossing Domain-wall Modes In An Aubry-André Model With Nonlocal Hopping
authors: Xiarui Zhan, Mingsheng Tian, Qiongyi He, Kaiye Shi, And Wei Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiarui Zhan, Mingsheng Tian, Qiongyi He, Kaiye Shi, and Wei Zhang

Nonequilibrium transport remains a central theme in modern physics, spanning from condensed matter to synthetic systems. Here, we investigate particle transport in an extended Aubry-André model with system-scale hopping, namely, nonlocal hopping with a range proportional to the system size, and unco…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033308] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies particle transport in an Aubry-André model with nonlocal hopping and reports metal-insulator coexistence and domain-wall modes.
motivation: To understand nonequilibrium transport in systems with long-range hopping, which is relevant to both condensed matter and synthetic systems.
method: The authors extend the Aubry-André model to include nonlocal hopping with range proportional to system size and analyze its transport properties.
result: They observe coexistence of metallic and insulating phases, as well as gap-crossing domain-wall modes.
conclusion: The findings may provide insights into transport phenomena in synthetic systems with engineered long-range couplings.

title: Universality In Fidelity-based Quantum Metrology
authors: Luis Aragón-Muñoz, Chryssomalis Chryssomalakos, Ana Gabriela Flores-Delgado, John Martin, And Eduardo Serrano-Ensástiga
abstract:
