We consider the problem of identifying the quantum spin states that are the optimal sensors of a given transformation, averaged over all possible orientations of the spin system. [Phys. Rev. A 114, 032406] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies optimal quantum spin states for sensing a given transformation averaged over all orientations using a fidelity criterion, demonstrating universality across unitary transformations.
motivation: The goal is to find quantum states that serve as optimal sensors for parameter estimation, irrespective of the specific unitary transformation or orientation, providing a general framework.
method: A geometric approach based on fidelity is used, encompassing any unitary transformation and averaging over all spin system orientations.
result: The paper reveals universal properties of optimal sensor states, with implications for quantum metrology.
conclusion: The fidelity-based method offers a general and geometric way to determine optimal probes for quantum measurements.

title: Interpreting Quantum-reference-frame Transformations Through A Simple Example
authors: Esteban Castro-Ruiz, Thomas D. Galley, And Leon Loveridge

tldr: This paper examines quantum reference frame transformations through a simple example to clarify and interpret differing frameworks.
motivation: Quantum reference frame transformations are ambiguous due to multiple proposed frameworks with conflicting rules; the authors seek to clarify by analyzing a simple case.
method: The authors take a simple example and apply different quantum reference frame transformation rules to compare and interpret the results.
result: The paper likely demonstrates how different frameworks produce divergent outcomes for the same situation, highlighting interpretational issues.
conclusion: The work aims to provide a clearer conceptual foundation for quantum reference frame transformations, potentially resolving ambiguities.

title: Multiatom Dipole-dipole Correlations In Rubidium Vapor Revealed By Dual-comb Spectroscopy
authors: Bachana Lomsadze, Roman Junes, And Johnason Yao

[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032801] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: This experimental paper studies dipole-dipole correlations among atoms in rubidium vapor using dual-comb spectroscopy, focusing on fundamental few-body effects rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To reveal multiatom correlations arising from dipole-dipole interactions in dilute atomic vapors, which are typically hidden in nonlinear spectroscopic signals.
method: Employed dual-comb spectroscopy to perform nonlinear measurements, isolating two-atom double-quantum coherences and higher-order multiatom responses.
result: Observed clear signatures of multiatom correlations, demonstrating the capability of the technique to access few-body interaction effects.
conclusion: The work provides a new spectroscopic platform for studying dipole-dipole interactions in atomic ensembles, potentially useful for many-body physics but not directly tied to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Resolving Magnetic-sublevel Structure In Rydberg Autler-Townes Spectra With Arbitrary Rf Polarization
authors: Noah Schlossberger, Rajavardhan Talashila, Stone B. Oliver, Nikunjkumar Prajapati, William J. Watterson, And Christopher L. Holloway

We investigate the role of magnetic sublevels in Autler-Townes spectra of Rydberg atoms driven by radio-frequency (rf) fields with arbitrary polarization. While conventional treatments predict two symmetric sidebands from independent [MATH] transitions, experiments have reported additional unexpl…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033701] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how magnetic sublevels affect Autler-Townes spectra in Rydberg atoms for arbitrary RF polarization, explaining additional observed features.
motivation: Conventional models predict only two symmetric sidebands, but experiments show unexplained features, so a more detailed model considering magnetic sublevels is needed.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the Autler-Townes spectra including magnetic sublevels and arbitrary RF polarization, likely with quantum mechanical calculations.
result: They show that magnetic sublevels produce additional spectral features, and their model resolves the discrepancy with experimental observations.

These jumps are commonly thought to require s…

motivation: To understand the conditions and dynamics of non-Hermitian jumps, which are unique to non-Hermitian systems and may have implications for open quantum systems.
method: The authors likely employ theoretical analysis and numerical simulations to study wave packet dynamics in disordered PT-symmetric systems.
result: They find that non-Hermitian jumps can occur under certain conditions, possibly relaxing previous assumptions about their prerequisites.
conclusion: The study provides insights into non-Hermitian dynamics and may be relevant for understanding effective descriptions of open quantum systems, though it is not directly connected to the researcher's core interests.

title: Grassmann Variational Monte Carlo With Neural Wave Functions
authors: Douglas Hendry, Alessandro Sinibaldi, And Giuseppe Carleo
abstract:
Author(s): Douglas Hendry, Alessandro Sinibaldi, and Giuseppe Carleo

Excited states play a central role in determining the physical properties of quantum matter, yet their accurate computation in many-body systems remains a formidable challenge for numerical methods. While neural quantum states have delivered outstanding results for ground-state problems, extending t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134404] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a Grassmann variational Monte Carlo method using neural wave functions to efficiently compute excited states of fermionic many-body systems.
motivation: Excited states are crucial for determining physical properties of quantum matter but are numerically challenging; neural quantum states have succeeded for ground states, so extending to excited states is a natural next step.
method: The authors develop a variational Monte Carlo approach that incorporates Grassmann (fermionic) variables into neural network wave functions to represent anti-symmetric states and compute excited states via variational optimization.
result: The method demonstrates accurate and efficient computation of excited states for several fermionic systems, potentially outperforming existing numerical approaches.
conclusion: This work expands the applicability of neural quantum states to excited states, offering a promising tool for studying quantum many-body systems beyond ground-state properties.

title: Quantum System Reliability: A Phase-encoded Interference Framework For Interdependent And Interconnected Systems
authors: S. Hooman Ghasemi
abstract:
Author(s): S. Hooman Ghasemi

Accurate reliability assessment of interconnected and interdependent systems requires explicit representation of interaction mechanisms arising from shared components, load redistribution, feedback coupling, and correlated degradation. Classical system reliability theory is formulated using real-val…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034301] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a phase-encoded interference framework to model reliability of interdependent and interconnected systems, aiming to overcome limitations of classical reliability theory.
motivation: Classical system reliability theory struggles to accurately represent complex interactions such as shared components, load redistribution, and feedback coupling in interconnected systems.
method: Proposes a quantum-inspired framework using phase-encoded interference to explicitly model interaction mechanisms and correlated degradation.
result: The framework offers a more realistic and accurate reliability assessment for interdependent systems compared to classical methods.
conclusion: Provides a novel tool for reliability engineering, though its connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, or networks is tenuous.

title: Noise-controlled Critical Slowing Down In Forced Neural And Climate Models
authors: Dianavinnarasi Joseph, Mithun Kumar, Suresh Kumarasamy, And Alexander N. Pisarchik
abstract:

Slowly forced nonlinear systems are known to exhibit delayed transitions beyond static bifurcation thresholds, a phenomenon that can be substantially modified by additive noise. tldr: This paper investigates how noise modulates critical slowing down and tipping points in forced nonlinear neural and climate models.
motivation: Understanding the impact of stochastic fluctuations on delayed transitions and tipping dynamics in slowly forced nonlinear systems.
method: The authors analyze two representative forced nonlinear systems (neural and climate models) under additive noise, presumably using stochastic differential equations and numerical simulations.
result: They find that noise can control the timing and occurrence of critical transitions, modifying bifurcation delay.
conclusion: The study provides insights into noise-induced behavior in complex systems, applicable to predicting sudden shifts in neural and climate dynamics.

title: Quantum Geometric Tensor For The Group Su(1,1)
authors: Tharon Holdsworth And Girish S. Agarwal
abstract:

tldr: This paper proposes a method to measure the quantum geometric tensor for systems with noncompact SU(1,1) symmetry using a double quench protocol.
motivation: To extend the measurement of quantum geometric properties, such as quantum metric and Berry curvature, to noncompact symmetry groups, which are important in many physical systems but less explored compared to compact groups.
method: The authors employ a double quench in parameter space to dynamically extract the quantum geometric tensor components for SU(1,1) symmetric systems.
result: They demonstrate a viable protocol for measuring the quantum geometric tensor in noncompact SU(1,1) systems, potentially enabling access to geometric and topological features.
conclusion: The work provides a new tool for probing quantum geometry in a broader class of systems, which may have implications for understanding geometric phases and topological properties.

title: Balancing quasi-Bragg Regime And Velocity Selectivity In Quantum-enhanced Atom Interferometry
authors: Christian M. Karres, Daniel Derr, And Enno Giese
abstract:
Author(s): Christian M. Karres, Daniel Derr, and Enno Giese

Spin squeezing in atomic ensembles enables atom interferometry with sensitivities below the shot-noise limit, but the associated entanglement is highly susceptible to loss, making imperfections in atom optics a central limitation. Bragg diffraction is an established technique for driving transitions…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033247] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how to balance the quasi-Bragg regime and velocity selectivity in atom interferometry to maintain sub-shot-noise sensitivity provided by spin squeezing despite realistic imperfections.
motivation: Spin squeezing can enhance atom interferometry beyond the shot-noise limit, but the fragile entanglement is highly susceptible to losses from imperfections in atom optics, particularly in Bragg diffraction.
method: The authors analyze the trade-off between quasi-Bragg diffraction and velocity selectivity, likely deriving conditions for optimal interferometer performance under realistic losses.
result: They identify a balancing condition that preserves quantum enhancement while mitigating the adverse effects of diffraction inefficiencies.
conclusion: By carefully choosing the diffraction regime, quantum-enhanced atom interferometry can be made more practical and robust to atom optic imperfections.

title: Metalearning Characteristics And Dynamics Of Quantum Systems
authors: Lucas Schorling, Pranav Vaidhyanathan, Jonas Schuff, Miguel J. Carballido, Dominik Zumbühl, Gerard Milburn, Florian Marquardt, Jakob Foerster, Maike Osborne, And Natalia Ares
abstract:

While machine learning holds great promise for quantum technologies, most current methods focus on predicting or controlling a specific quantum system. motivation: Current ML methods are specific to single systems; metalearning can leverage knowledge from previous data to adapt to new systems.
method: They likely develop a metalearning approach that learns to learn across multiple quantum systems.
result: The metalearning approach generalizes to unseen quantum systems from few examples.
conclusion: Metalearning offers a promising route for applying machine learning to diverse quantum systems efficiently.

title: Probing Excited-state Quantum Phase Transitions With Trapped Cold Ions
authors: Marek Kuchař And Michal Macek
abstract:

We propose concrete protocols to realize quantum criticality due to excited-state quantum phase transitions (ESQPTs) experimentally in presumably the simplest and most resilient system involving a single trapped ion oscillating in a radio-frequency Paul trap. We identify a specific class of excited …

tldr: Proposes experimental protocols using a single trapped ion to realize and observe excited-state quantum phase transitions (ESQPTs).
motivation: To provide an experimentally feasible and simple platform for studying ESQPTs, which are theoretically predicted but challenging to observe.
method: Identifies a specific class of excited states in a single trapped ion in a Paul trap and designs laser-driven protocols to probe the critical behavior.
result: The proposed protocols are concrete and use a resilient single-ion system, potentially enabling direct experimental observation of ESQPT signatures.
conclusion: A trapped ion can serve as an ideal testbed for investigating excited-state quantum criticality, bridging theory and experiment.

title: Optical Cycling On Thorium Monoxide For An Improved Test Of Fundamental Symmetries

tldr: The paper demonstrates optical cycling in thorium monoxide, enabling enhanced tests of fundamental symmetry violations.
motivation: Optical cycling in molecules enables quantum control and readout techniques, which are essential for high-precision measurements of fundamental symmetries, such as the search for the electron electric dipole moment.
method: The authors likely employ laser cooling and repumping schemes on an electronic transition of thorium monoxide to achieve multiple photon scattering cycles.
result: The work reports successful optical cycling and improved sensitivity for symmetry tests in a molecule that is particularly sensitive to new physics.
conclusion: This achievement paves the way for next-generation experiments probing fundamental symmetry violations and the electric dipole moment of the electron.

title: Ab Initio Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo In The Thermodynamic Limit

result: The method achieves accurate simulations of real quantum materials, demonstrating its potential.

title: Securing Elliptic Curve Cryptocurrencies Against Quantum Vulnerabilities: Resource Estimates And Mitigations
authors: Ryan Babbush, Adam Zalcman, Craig Gidney, Michael Broughton, Tanuj Khattar, Hartmut Neven, Thiago Bergamaschi, Justin Drake, And Dan Boneh
abstract:

[PRX Quantum 7, 031001] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.

motivation: To assess the practical threat of quantum computers to elliptic curve cryptography used in cryptocurrencies and highlight the urgency of adopting post-quantum standards.
method: The authors provide detailed resource estimates for quantum attacks (likely via Shor's algorithm) on elliptic curve cryptography, analyzing the computational requirements and discussing potential mitigations.

conclusion: The community must urgently transition to post-quantum cryptographic primitives to secure cryptocurrency systems.

title: Optical Thermodynamics Beyond The Weak Nonlinearity Limit

Optical thermodynamics has recently emerged as a theoretical framework describing a Rayleigh-Jeans (RJ) modal power distribution of multimoded nonlinear photonic circuits. However, its applicability is constrained to systems exhibiting weak nonlinear mode-mode interactions. Here, by employing a tran…

tldr: This paper extends the framework of optical thermodynamics beyond the weak nonlinearity limit in multimoded nonlinear photonic circuits.
motivation: The existing optical thermodynamics theory describing Rayleigh-Jeans modal power distributions is limited to weak nonlinear interactions; the authors aim to generalize it to stronger nonlinear regimes.

result: The work demonstrates that optical thermodynamics holds beyond the weak nonlinearity limit, providing a broader theoretical foundation for such systems.

authors: Egor I. Kiselev

method: The study likely applies quantum mechanical principles and constraints to analyze the proposed neutrino-laser scheme involving radioactive decay in a BEC.

tldr: The paper shows that an electric field can create potential wells between ultracold polar molecules in nonadjacent rotational states, supporting field-linked tetratomic states and enabling tunable elastic collisions.
motivation: Controlling ultracold molecular interactions is key for quantum applications; this work explores electric-field tuning as a mechanism.
method: The authors analyze the electric-field-induced potential energy surface and compute the resulting scattering properties (e.g., elastic cross sections).
result: They find that within experimentally accessible field strengths, the potential well is deep enough to support tetratomic bound states, leading to highly tunable elastic cross sections.
conclusion: This offers a new handle for controlling ultracold molecular collisions, with potential relevance to quantum simulation and precision measurements.

motivation: The authors aim to accurately describe the ground state properties of quantum gases with long-range interactions mediated by a cavity, which is of interest for understanding many-body physics in such systems.
method: They employ Variational and Diffusion Monte Carlo methods, using a nontranslationally invariant Jastrow wave function derived from the exact two-body solution.
result: The study likely provides accurate ground-state energies and structural properties for the gas, capturing the effects of cavity-mediated interactions.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of quantum gases with infinite-range interactions, though it is primarily a condensed-matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information processing, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined.

tldr: This paper presents a variational Monte Carlo method using row-update projected entangled-pair states (PEPS) to compute ground states of quantum spin glasses.
motivation: Quantum many-body ground-state problems, especially for frustrated and disordered systems like quantum spin glasses, remain computationally challenging.
method: The authors develop a row-update PEPS variational Monte Carlo scheme to optimize tensor network states for quantum spin glass models.
result: The method is applied to quantum spin glasses, likely demonstrating accurate ground-state energies and insights into the physics of these systems.
conclusion: The proposed PEPS-based variational Monte Carlo approach is an effective numerical tool for studying quantum spin glasses, which are difficult to simulate with other methods.

title: Qudit-native Framework For Discrete Time Crystals

result: Qudit-based DTCs exhibit distinct and robust dynamical features not present in qubit systems.
conclusion: The framework offers a new approach to DTC engineering, with potential implications for quantum simulations and metrology.

title: Finite Dissipation Anomaly In Collisionless Plasma Turbulence
authors: Riddhi Bandyopadhyay, Subash Adhikari, Yan Yang, And William H. Matthaeus
abstract:

A key principle underlying most turbulence theories is that the mean energy dissipation rate remains finite even as viscosity vanishes: the so-called zeroth law of turbulence. Although this property has been established for hydrodynamic and magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence, its validity in weakl…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035202] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the zeroth law of turbulence in collisionless plasma, showing that finite energy dissipation persists even as viscosity vanishes.
motivation: To determine whether the universal property of finite dissipation in turbulent systems applies to weakly collisional plasmas, which are prevalent in space and astrophysical contexts.
method: The authors likely employ theoretical analysis and/or numerical simulations of plasma turbulence within a kinetic or fluid framework to examine scaling of energy dissipation as collisionality decreases.
result: The paper reports that finite dissipation is achieved even in collisionless plasma turbulence, indicating the anomaly holds, likely through collisionless mechanisms such as Landau damping or phase mixing.
conclusion: The zeroth law of turbulence extends to collisionless plasmas, implying that turbulent dissipation in such media is independent of collisionality and is intrinsic to nonlinear cascade processes.

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032039] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that Coulomb interactions in a trivial moiré band can stabilize a Laughlin-like fractional Chern insulator, revealing that many-body topology can arise from quantum geometry alone.
motivation: Fractional Chern insulators are typically associated with topologically nontrivial bands, but this work challenges that assumption by exploring the possibility of such states in trivial bands, which could broaden the search for topological phases.
method: The authors theoretically study realistic Coulomb interactions in moiré graphene, likely using numerical exact diagonalization or similar techniques to examine the many-body ground state.

conclusion: The existence of many-body topological order does not require band topology, and quantum geometry alone can stabilize fractional Chern insulators, which has implications for the design of topological quantum matter.

title: Spin Inertia As A Source Of Topological Magnons: Chiral Edge States From Coupled Precession And Nutation

tldr: The paper shows that spin inertia in a honeycomb ferromagnet creates topologically nontrivial magnon bands with chiral edge states.
motivation: To explore whether spin inertia, an often-neglected effect, can generate topological magnon bands and chiral edge states.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a honeycomb ferromagnet including spin inertia, compute Chern numbers, and simulate slab geometries to identify edge modes.
result: Spin inertia hybridizes precessional and nutational magnon bands, opening a topologically nontrivial gap that scales linearly with pseudodipolar interaction strength, yielding chiral edge modes.
conclusion: Spin inertia provides a new mechanism for realizing topological magnon states, with potential implications for spintronics and magnonics.

[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024155] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the crossover from generalized hydrodynamics to conventional hydrodynamics in nearly integrable systems, using a relaxation time approximation to simplify the Boltzmann collision term.
motivation: Understanding how integrability breaking leads to the emergence of conventional hydrodynamics from the generalized hydrodynamics description of integrable systems.
method: The authors consider a simplified version of the Boltzmann collision term, adopting a relaxation time approximation, and analyze the resulting equations to study the crossover behavior.
result: The paper likely reveals how the relaxation time approximation captures the crossover from ballistic (GHD) to diffusive (conventional) transport.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the transition from integrable to non-integrable dynamics and the validity of hydrodynamic descriptions.

title: Stable Three-dimensional Solitons In Spin-orbit-coupled Atomic-molecular Condensates
authors: Chao Kong, Jinqing Li, Guihua Chen, Guilong Li, Zhaopin Chen, Haiming Deng, Boris A. Malomed, And Yongyao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Kong, Jinqing Li, Guihua Chen, Guilong Li, Zhaopin Chen, Haiming Deng, Boris A. Malomed, and Yongyao Li

We elaborate a mechanism for the creation of stable three-dimensional (3D) solitons in spin-orbit-coupled (SOC) atomic-molecular Bose-Einstein condensates, modeled by the mean-field equations with the quadratic three-wave interaction, characterized by mismatch [MATH]. The planar (effectively two-dimens…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033278] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a mechanism for creating stable three-dimensional solitons in spin-orbit-coupled atomic-molecular Bose-Einstein condensates using mean-field equations with quadratic three-wave interaction.
motivation: To address the challenge of stabilizing 3D solitons in Bose-Einstein condensates, which are typically fragile, by leveraging spin-orbit coupling and atomic-molecular conversion.
method: The authors model the condensate using mean-field equations that include quadratic three-wave interactions with mismatch, and analyze the existence and stability of solitonic solutions.
result: They elaborate a mechanism that allows for the creation of stable 3D solitons, extending previous work on lower-dimensional solitons in such systems.
conclusion: Stable 3D solitons can be realized in spin-orbit-coupled atomic-molecular condensates, offering new possibilities for nonlinear matter-wave studies.

title: Quantum Limit Cycles With Continuous Symmetries From Coherent Parametric Driving: Exact Solutions And Many-body Extensions
authors: Sihan Chen And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Sihan Chen and Aashish A. Clerk

There is widespread interest in many-body quantum systems that exhibit limit-cycle or time-crystalline behavior. An ideal quantum limit cycle would be realized using fully coherent driving (to minimize noise) and also have a continuous internal symmetry (to ensure generation of monochromatic radiati…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033264] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically explores quantum limit cycles with continuous symmetries generated by coherent parametric driving, providing exact solutions and many-body extensions.
motivation: There is interest in many-body quantum systems showing limit-cycle or time-crystalline behavior; an ideal quantum limit cycle would use fully coherent driving and have continuous internal symmetry to generate monochromatic radiation.
method: The authors develop exact theoretical models for coherently driven quantum systems exhibiting limit cycles, then extend these models to many-body systems.
result: They obtain exact solutions for the limit cycle dynamics and characterize the stability and synchronization properties, including extensions to many-body systems that exhibit time-crystalline behavior.

title: Nonlinear Viscoelastoplastic Rheology Of A Viscous Vertex Model
authors: Shalabh K. Anand And Matthias Merkel
abstract:
Author(s): Shalabh K. Anand and Matthias Merkel

Morphogenesis involves complex shape changes of biological tissues. Yet, tissue shape changes depend on tissue rheology, which in turn arises from the interplay of large numbers of cells. Here, we link cell- and tissue-scale mechanics by constructing mean-field rheological relations for the vertex m…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033263] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: Construction of mean-field rheological relations for a viscous vertex model to describe nonlinear viscoelastoplastic behavior of biological tissues.
motivation: Tissue shape changes during morphogenesis depend on tissue rheology, which arises from cell-scale interactions. Linking cell and tissue mechanics is essential.
method: The authors construct mean-field rheological relations based on a viscous vertex model, incorporating viscoelastic and plastic deformation mechanisms.
result: The paper derives analytical expressions that capture tissue viscoelastoplastic rheology, enabling predictions of tissue behavior under deformation.
conclusion: The proposed model provides a framework to understand how cell-level properties influence tissue-scale mechanics during morphogenesis.

title: International Optical Clock Comparison Using The European Optical Fiber Network
authors: Marco Pizzocaro et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Pizzocaro et al.

Optical clocks have achieved remarkable estimated fractional frequency uncertainties reaching the [MATH] level and below, enabling applications in fundamental physics, general relativity, and geodesy. However, the challenge of verifying the international consistency of optical clocks remains c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033250] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates international comparison of optical clocks using the European optical fiber network to verify their consistency.
motivation: To verify the international consistency of optical clocks and support applications in fundamental physics, geodesy, and general relativity, requiring remote comparisons.
method: The authors used the European optical fiber network to link multiple optical clocks and performed frequency comparisons across international distances.
result: The comparisons achieved uncertainties at a level consistent with the clocks' performance, demonstrating the network's capability for global clock comparisons.
conclusion: The European fiber network enables reliable international comparisons of optical clocks, which is important for future redefinitions of the second and high-precision metrology.

title: Fast-forwardability Of Qubit-mapped Fermion Models Based On Cartan Decomposition
authors: Yuichiro Hidaka, Shoichiro Tsutsui, Shota Kanasugi, Norifumi Matsumoto, Kazunori Maruyama, And Hirotaka Oshima
abstract:
Author(s): Yuichiro Hidaka, Shoichiro Tsutsui, Shota Kanasugi, Norifumi Matsumoto, Kazunori Maruyama, and Hirotaka Oshima

We study the Hamiltonian algebra of qubit-mapped interacting fermion models and their fast-forwardability. We prove that the dimension of the Hamiltonian algebra of the fermion model with single-site Coulomb interaction is bounded from below by the exponential function of the number of sites, and th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033251] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the Hamiltonian algebra of qubit-mapped fermion models and proves an exponential lower bound on its dimension, suggesting that fast-forwarding such systems is generally infeasible.
motivation: The work aims to understand the computational complexity of simulating interacting fermion models on a quantum computer, specifically whether their time evolution can be efficiently fast-forwarded.
method: The authors employ Cartan decomposition to characterize the Hamiltonian algebra and derive lower bounds on its dimension for models with single-site Coulomb interaction.
result: The dimension of the Hamiltonian algebra is shown to grow exponentially with the number of sites, even for the specific case of single-site Coulomb interaction.
conclusion: The exponential growth implies that fast-forwarding is not possible in general, highlighting inherent simulation costs for such fermionic models.

title: Oracle Problems As Communication Tasks And Optimization Of Quantum Algorithms
authors: Amit Te’eni, Zohar Schwartzman-Nowik, Marcin Nowakowski, Paweł Horodecki, And Eliahu Cohen
abstract:
Author(s): Amit Te’eni, Zohar Schwartzman-Nowik, Marcin Nowakowski, Paweł Horodecki, and Eliahu Cohen

Quantum query complexity studies the number of queries needed to learn some property of a black box. A closely related question is how well an algorithm can succeed with this learning task using only a fixed number of queries. In this work, we propose measuring an algorithm's performance using the m…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033252] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a new measure for quantum algorithm performance in oracle problems, recasting them as communication tasks.
motivation: Quantum query complexity is fundamental, but existing measures focus on query count; the authors aim to refine algorithm evaluation when query count is fixed.
method: By reformulating oracle problems as communication tasks, they introduce a performance metric based on success probability with limited queries.
result: The framework likely provides new bounds or optimization strategies for quantum algorithms, though full details are unavailable from the abstract.
conclusion: The work contributes to quantum query complexity and algorithm optimization, but is outside the specified research directions.

title: Marginally Volume-dependent Oscillation Modes Of Superfluid Pendant Droplets In An Intervening Stability Region
authors: Ryota Yamane, Shota Takamatsu, Yuri Ishimoto, Keito Miyake, Tomoyuki Tani, Yuki Aoki, And Ryuji Nomura
abstract:
Author(s): Ryota Yamane, Shota Takamatsu, Yuri Ishimoto, Keito Miyake, Tomoyuki Tani, Yuki Aoki, and Ryuji Nomura

Droplets are ubiquitous in nature and industry, yet their behavior is not yet fully understood, particularly for extreme conditions not typically encountered in viscous classical fluids. In this study, we investigated the oscillations of a superfluid [MATH] pendant droplet formed beneath …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033255] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates oscillation modes of superfluid pendant droplets, finding marginally volume-dependent modes in a stability region.
motivation: To understand droplet behavior under extreme conditions not typical for viscous classical fluids, using superfluids as a quantum fluid.
method: Experimental study of pendant superfluid droplets, likely involving imaging and analysis of oscillation frequencies to extract mode behavior.
result: Identification of oscillation modes whose frequencies depend on droplet volume only marginally within a particular stability region.
conclusion: The results provide new insights into the dynamics of superfluid droplets, contributing to fundamental understanding of quantum fluid behavior.

title: Robust Correlation-induced Localization Under Time-reversal Symmetry Breaking
authors: Bikram Pain, Sthitadhi Roy, Jens H. Bardarson, And Ivan M. Khaymovich
abstract:
Author(s): Bikram Pain, Sthitadhi Roy, Jens H. Bardarson, and Ivan M. Khaymovich

The correlation-induced localization, that is, the Anderson localization in long-range models with correlated hopping, is found to be robust to time-reversal symmetry (TRS) breaking up to a certain critical TRS breaking parameter. It is also shown that, unlike eigenstate localization properties, the wave-packet dynamics is fragile to any TRS breaking and undergoes a transition from subdiffusion at TRS to diffusion otherwise.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032037] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the impact of time-reversal symmetry breaking on correlation-induced localization in long-range hopping models, finding robust eigenstate localization but fragile wave-packet dynamics.
motivation: To understand whether correlation-induced localization persists when time-reversal symmetry is broken, which is relevant for the stability of localization phenomena in quantum systems.
method: The authors likely analyze a model with correlated hopping, introduce a TRS-breaking parameter, and study both eigenstate properties and wave-packet dynamics.
result: Eigenstate localization is robust up to a critical TRS-breaking strength, whereas wave-packet dynamics transitions from subdiffusion to diffusion for any finite breaking.
conclusion: The study reveals a distinction between static and dynamic localization properties under symmetry breaking, contributing to the understanding of localization robustness.

title: Complete Classification Of Integrability And Nonintegrability For Spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Chain With Symmetric Nearest-neighbor Interaction
authors: Mizuki Sanatani, Yuuya Chiba, And Naoto Shiraishi
abstract:
Author(s): Mizuki Sanatani, Yuuya Chiba, and Naoto Shiraishi

General spin-[MATH] chains with symmetric nearest-neighbor interaction are studied. We rigorously prove that all spin models in this class, except for known integrable systems, are nonintegrable in the sense that they possess no nontrivial local conserved quantities. This result confirms that…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033240] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously classifies spin-1/2 chains with symmetric nearest-neighbor interactions, proving that all models except known integrable cases lack local conserved quantities, confirming nonintegrability.
motivation: To determine which spin-1/2 chains with symmetric nearest-neighbor interactions are integrable, and to prove nonintegrability for the rest by showing absence of local conserved quantities.
method: The authors employ rigorous mathematical proofs to analyze the existence of local conserved quantities for general spin-1/2 chains with symmetric nearest-neighbor interactions.
result: They prove that all such chains except for known integrable systems possess no nontrivial local conserved quantities, leading to a complete classification of integrability and nonintegrability in this class.
conclusion: This work establishes which spin-1/2 chains are integrable and confirms nonintegrability for all others, advancing understanding of quantum many-body systems.

title: Model-free Detection Of Physical Order From Scattering And Imaging Data Using Escort-weighted Shannon Entropy And Divergence Matrices
authors: Jared Coles, Arthur R. C. Mccray, Yue Li, Bryan T. Fichera, Yan Wu, Yiqing Hao, Daniel Phelan, Yue Cao, Raymond Osborn, Charudatta Phatak, Stephan Rosenkranz, And Yu Li
abstract:
Author(s): Jared Coles, Arthur R. C. McCray, Yue Li, Bryan T. Fichera, Yan Wu, Yiqing Hao, Daniel Phelan, Yue Cao, Raymond Osborn, Charudatta Phatak, Stephan Rosenkranz, and Yu Li

We demonstrate a model-free data analysis framework that leverages escort-weighted Shannon entropy and several divergence matrices to detect phase transitions in scattering and imaging datasets. By establishing a connection between physical entropy and informational entropy, this approach provides a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033235] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a model-free data analysis framework using escort-weighted Shannon entropy to detect phase transitions in scattering and imaging data.
motivation: To provide a general method for identifying physical order without relying on specific models, applicable to diverse experimental datasets.
method: The approach connects physical entropy with informational entropy using escort-weighted Shannon entropy and divergence matrices to analyze scattering and imaging data.
result: The framework successfully detects phase transitions in the tested datasets, demonstrating its utility as a model-free diagnostic tool.
conclusion: The method offers a versatile, model-agnostic way to identify phase transitions from experimental data, though its connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is not established.

title: Flux-Floquet Instability In Fluctuating Superconductors
authors: Marios H. Michael, Duilio de Santis, Eugene A. Demler, And Patrick A. Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Marios H. Michael, Duilio De Santis, Eugene A. Demler, and Patrick A. Lee

Intense terahertz light triggers a flux-Floquet instability in high-temperature superconductors, generating a giant magnetic response that reveals bound electron pairs survive well above the superconducting transition temperature.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031055] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: Intense terahertz light triggers a flux-Floquet instability in high-temperature superconductors, generating a giant magnetic response that reveals bound electron pairs survive above the superconducting transition temperature.
motivation: To investigate the response of high-temperature superconductors to intense terahertz radiation and to understand whether Cooper pairs persist above the critical temperature.
method: The study likely combines experimental terahertz driving of superconductors with theoretical analysis of flux-Floquet instabilities to explain the observed magnetic response.
result: A giant magnetic response is induced by the flux-Floquet instability, indicating that bound electron pairs exist well above the superconducting transition temperature.
conclusion: The findings suggest that preformed Cooper pairs survive above Tc and that terahertz driving can reveal and manipulate such pairing, offering insights into high-Tc superconductivity.

title: Particle View Of Many-Body Electronic Structure With Neural Network Wave Function
authors: Zichen Wang, Weizhong Fu, Zhe Li, Weiluo Ren, And Ji Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zichen Wang, Weizhong Fu, Zhe Li, Weiluo Ren, and Ji Chen

A combination of theoretical approaches bridges the gap between complex quantum wave functions and the classical picture of electron positions for molecules and solids.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031048] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper bridges complex quantum wave functions with classical electron positions for molecules and solids using neural network wave functions.
motivation: To provide a particle-based interpretation of many-body electronic structure, enhancing understanding of complex quantum states.
method: The study combines theoretical approaches with neural network wave function techniques to map quantum wave functions to classical electron positions.
result: The work demonstrates a bridge between quantum wave functions and classical pictures, likely enabling new insights into molecular and solid systems.
conclusion: The approach offers a novel way to visualize and understand many-body electronic structure through a particle view.

title: Bulklike Costless Domain Walls Driven By Phonon Pair Condensation In ${\mathrm{HfO}}_{2}$
authors: Hyun-Jae Lee, Pawan Kumar, Kyoung-June Go, Chang Hoon Kim, Yungyeom Kim, Kyoungjun Lee, Takao Shimizu, Seung Chul Chae, Hosub Jin, Minseong Lee, Umesh Waghmare, Si-Young Choi, And Jun Hee Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Hyun-Jae Lee, Pawan Kumar, Kyoung-June Go, Chang Hoon Kim, Yungyeom Kim, Kyoungjun Lee, Takao Shimizu, Seung Chul Chae, Hosub Jin, Minseong Lee, Umesh Waghmare, Si-Young Choi, and Jun Hee Lee

A previously unrecognized governing principle helps to explain the stable electrical properties in some ferroelectric materials like hafnium oxide.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031041] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies a phonon pair condensation mechanism that leads to costless domain walls in HfO2, explaining its stable ferroelectric properties.
motivation: To understand why HfO2 exhibits stable ferroelectricity despite structural complexities, which is important for applications.
method: Likely first-principles calculations (e.g., DFT) to study phonon modes and domain wall formation energies.
result: They found that condensation of phonon pairs results in bulklike domain walls that cost no energy, explaining the robustness of ferroelectricity.
conclusion: This new principle provides insight into ferroelectric stability in HfO2 and related materials.

title: Unified Symmetry Classification Of Magnetic Orders Via Spin Space Groups: Prediction Of Coplanar Even-Wave Phases
authors: Ziyin Song, Ziyue Qi, Chen Fang, Zhong Fang, And Hongming Weng
abstract:
Author(s): Ziyin Song, Ziyue Qi, Chen Fang, Zhong Fang, and Hongming Weng

A unified classification framework based on spin space group symmetry predicts a coplanar even-wave magnetic phase where electronic band spin polarization varies continuously and can vanish without band degeneracy.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031038] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified classification of magnetic orders using spin space groups, predicting a coplanar even-wave phase with continuously varying spin polarization.
motivation: Conventional crystallographic groups are insufficient to describe all magnetic symmetries, motivating a broader framework based on spin space groups to systematically classify and predict novel magnetic phases.
method: The authors develop a unified classification formalism based on spin space group symmetry, which explicitly considers spin and spatial rotations independently, and apply it to search for new magnetic orders.
result: They predict a coplanar even-wave magnetic phase where the electronic band spin polarization varies continuously and can vanish without requiring band degeneracy, a qualitatively new type of magnetic order.
conclusion: The spin space group framework significantly extends the classification of magnetic structures and could guide the discovery of materials with unconventional magnetic behavior.

title: Strain-Tunable Anomalous Hall Effect In Hexagonal MnTe
authors: Zhaoyu Liu, Sijie Xu, Jonathan M. Destefano, Elliott Rosenberg, Tingjun Zhang, Jinyulin Li, Matthew B. Stone, Feng Ye, Wei Tian, Sarah Edwards, Rong Cong, Siyu Pan, Ching-Wu Chu, Liangzi Deng, Emilia Morosan, Rafael M. Fernandes, Jiun-Haw Chu, And Pengcheng Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Liu, Sijie Xu, Jonathan M. DeStefano, Elliott Rosenberg, Tingjun Zhang, Jinyulin Li, Matthew B. Stone, Feng Ye, Wei Tian, Sarah Edwards, Rong Cong, Siyu Pan, Ching-Wu Chu, Liangzi Deng, Emilia Morosan, Rafael M. Fernandes, Jiun-Haw Chu, and Pengcheng Dai

Uniaxial strain applied to the hexagonal altermagnet
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031033] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the anomalous Hall effect in hexagonal MnTe, an altermagnet, and shows that uniaxial strain isolates a single magnetic domain and induces a sign reversal of the effect due to modifications in the Berry curvature.
motivation: To understand and control the anomalous Hall effect in altermagnets, which are a newly identified class of magnetic materials with potential applications in spintronics.
method: The authors apply uniaxial strain to MnTe crystals and measure the anomalous Hall effect, complemented by neutron scattering and transport measurements.
result: Strain application results in a sharp anomalous Hall effect and a sign reversal, demonstrating that strain tunes the electronic Berry curvature and magnetic domain structure.
conclusion: The findings reveal that strain is an effective tool to manipulate magnetic and electronic properties in altermagnets, which may be relevant for future device technologies.

title: Pseudogap, Fermi Liquid, Van Hove Singularity, And Maxima Of The Compressibility And Of The Knight Shift As A Function Of Doping In The Two-Dimensional Hubbard Model
authors: Y. M. Vilk And A.-M. S. Tremblay
abstract:
Author(s): Y. M. Vilk and A.-M. S. Tremblay

Analysis of Hubbard model simulations reveals that a maximum in the isothermal compressibility marks the pseudogap boundary, driven by spin-density-wave precursor bands crossing the zero-frequency level.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031034] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: A study of the two-dimensional Hubbard model showing that compressibility maxima mark the pseudogap boundary, arising from spin-density-wave precursor bands.
motivation: To understand the relationship between thermodynamic quantities and the pseudogap phase in strongly correlated systems.
method: Analysis of Hubbard model simulations, likely using numerical techniques, to compute isothermal compressibility across doping.
result: A maximum in the isothermal compressibility is found to coincide with the pseudogap boundary, driven by spin-density-wave precursor bands crossing zero frequency.
conclusion: The results suggest a thermodynamic signature of the pseudogap, potentially useful for interpreting experiments.

title: Fast Algorithm For 2d Rigidity Percolation
authors: Nina Javerzat And Daniele Notarmuzi
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Javerzat and Daniele Notarmuzi

An algorithm for simulating the rigidity percolation transition, based on novel theoretical results, overcomes previous size limitations and enables the highly precise characterization of its universality classes, shedding new light on rigidity transitions in amorphous systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031032] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a fast algorithm for simulating 2D rigidity percolation based on new theoretical results, enabling precise characterization of universality classes and insights into rigidity transitions in amorphous systems.
motivation: Previous algorithms faced size limitations that prevented highly precise characterization of the rigidity percolation transition, especially in amorphous systems.
method: The algorithm leverages novel theoretical results to overcome these size limitations, allowing for large-scale simulations.
result: The new algorithm enables highly precise characterization of universality classes and provides new insights into rigidity percolation transitions.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of rigidity percolation in two dimensions, with implications for amorphous materials, but it is unrelated to the specified quantum information research directions.

title: Path-Dependency And Emergent Computing Under Vectorial Driving
authors: C. M. Meulblok, A. Singh, M. Labousse, And M. van Hecke
abstract:
Author(s): C. M. Meulblok, A. Singh, M. Labousse, and M. van Hecke

A general framework unravels path dependencies across a wide range of driven complex materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031023] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: Presents a general framework for understanding path dependencies in driven complex materials, with implications for emergent computing.
motivation: Path dependency is a key feature of driven complex materials, enabling memory and computational behavior; a unified framework is needed to describe these phenomena across diverse systems.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework that analyzes path dependencies under vectorial driving, likely by mapping the system's response to driving protocols and identifying universal features.
result: The framework successfully captures path dependencies across a wide range of driven complex materials, suggesting general principles and potentially enabling emergent computing applications.
conclusion: This work provides a unifying perspective on path dependency in complex materials and opens new directions for using such systems as computational substrates, though the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is not established.

title: Deceleration Of Accelerator-Produced And In-Trap Electron Cooling Of Highly Charged Ions
authors: S. Rausch, Z. Andelkovic, S. Fedotova, W. Geithner, F. Herfurth, M. Horst, J. Ködel, K. Mohr, D. Neidherr, W. Nörtershäuser, N. Stallkamp, S. Trotsenko, G. Vorobjev, And D. Zisis
abstract:
Author(s): S. Rausch, Z. Andelkovic, S. Fedotova, W. Geithner, F. Herfurth, M. Horst, J. Ködel, K. Mohr, D. Neidherr, W. Nörtershäuser, N. Stallkamp, S. Trotsenko, G. Vorobjev, and D. Zisis

The electron cooling of highly charged ions (HCI) in a Penning trap, as well as the deceleration and trapping of accelerator-produced HCI, has been demonstrated at the HITRAP facility, paving the way for unprecedented precision experiments in QED, materials science, and astrophysics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031022] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates deceleration and in-trap electron cooling of highly charged ions at HITRAP for precision experiments.
motivation: To enable precision experiments in QED, materials science, and astrophysics using slow, cool highly charged ions.
method: Experimental implementation of deceleration and in-trap electron cooling of accelerator-produced HCI in a Penning trap at the HITRAP facility.
result: Successful demonstration of both deceleration and electron cooling, providing a platform for future precision measurements.
conclusion: The techniques validate the HITRAP approach and open avenues for high-accuracy studies in fundamental physics.

title: Non-Hermitian Bethe-Salpeter Equation For Open Systems: Emergence Of Exceptional Points In Excitonic Spectra From First Principles
authors: Zhenlin Zhang, Wei Hu, Enrico Perfetto, And Gianluca Stefanucci
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenlin Zhang, Wei Hu, Enrico Perfetto, and Gianluca Stefanucci

Extension of the Bethe-Salpeter equation to open quantum systems predicts that engineered photonic environments induce exceptional points in the excitonic spectra of transition-metal dichalcogenides, providing a pathway for non-Hermitian quantum devices with controllable optical and valleytronic properties.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031020] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: Extends the Bethe-Salpeter equation to open quantum systems, predicting exceptional points in excitonic spectra of transition-metal dichalcogenides for non-Hermitian quantum devices.
motivation: To explore non-Hermitian effects in excitonic systems and propose engineered photonic environments as a pathway for controllable optical and valleytronic quantum devices.
method: First-principles derivation of a non-Hermitian Bethe-Salpeter equation for open quantum systems, applied to transition-metal dichalcogenides.
result: Predicts the emergence of exceptional points in the excitonic spectra due to coupling with photonic environments.
conclusion: The work offers a theoretical foundation for designing non-Hermitian quantum devices with tunable optical and valleytronic properties.

title: Interaction-Driven Topological Transitions In Monolayer ${\mathrm{TaIrTe}}_{4}$
authors: Jiangxu Li, Jian Tang, Cheng Xu, Louis Primeau, Thomas Siyuan Ding, Rahul Soni, Tiema Qian, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ni Ni, Adrian Del Maestro, Qiong Ma, And Yang Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Jiangxu Li, Jian Tang, Cheng Xu, Louis Primeau, Thomas Siyuan Ding, Rahul Soni, Tiema Qian, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ni Ni, Adrian Del Maestro, Qiong Ma, and Yang Zhang

Theoretical and experimental mapping of monolayer TaIrTe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031017] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper maps interaction-driven topological phases in monolayer TaIrTe4, revealing a rich landscape without needing moiré engineering.
motivation: To understand how electron interactions drive topological transitions in a naturally layered material, potentially offering a simpler platform for topological physics.
method: Combines theoretical mapping (likely first-principles calculations) with experimental measurements on monolayer TaIrTe4.
result: Identifies multiple interaction-driven topological phases in the monolayer material.
conclusion: Electron interactions can produce topological transitions in monolayer TaIrTe4, providing a new material for studying topological phenomena.

title: Limits Of Inference In Complex Systems: When Stochastic Models Become Indistinguishable
authors: Javier Aguilar, Miguel A. Muñoz, And Sandro Azaele
abstract:
Author(s): Javier Aguilar, Miguel A. Muñoz, and Sandro Azaele

A path-inference framework quantifies data resolution limits that render distinct stochastic models empirically indistinguishable and offers guidelines for designing experimental measurements that maximize information extraction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031015] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: Develops a path-inference framework to determine data resolution limits at which different stochastic models become empirically indistinguishable, and provides guidelines for designing measurements to maximize information extraction.
motivation: To understand how limited data resolution affects the ability to distinguish among stochastic models in complex systems, and to optimize experimental design for maximum information gain.
method: The paper introduces a path-inference framework that quantifies the resolution limits leading to model indistinguishability.
result: The framework yields quantitative limits on model distinguishability and offers practical guidelines for experimental measurements.
conclusion: Empirical indistinguishability is fundamentally limited by data resolution, but can be mitigated by optimizing measurement design to extract maximal information.

title: Holographic Duality Between Bulk Topological Order And Boundary Mixed-State Order
authors: Tsung-Cheng Lu, Yu-Jie Liu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, And Yizhi You
abstract:
Author(s): Tsung-Cheng Lu, Yu-Jie Liu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, and Yizhi You

Mapping open quantum systems to higher-dimensional topological order provides a new framework for characterizing strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033041] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a holographic duality between bulk topological order and boundary mixed-state order, offering a framework to characterize strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases.
motivation: To understand and characterize quantum phases in open systems, particularly mixed-state order and symmetry breaking, using powerful tools from higher-dimensional topological phases.
method: The authors likely employ holographic mappings or dualities that relate boundary mixed quantum states to bulk topological order, possibly leveraging exact tensor network or renormalization group techniques.
result: The framework reveals a correspondence that connects properties of open quantum systems, such as strong-to-weak symmetry breaking, to topological order in one higher dimension, providing a new perspective on nonequilibrium phases.
conclusion: The duality offers a novel tool for classifying and interpreting mixed-state quantum phases, with potential implications for understanding quantum information in open systems.

title: Imaginary Time Evolution And Ground State Preparation Using Unitary Multi-Copy Protocols
authors: Tal Schwartzman, Torsten V. Zache, Hannes Pichler, And H. R. Sadeghpour
abstract:
Author(s): Tal Schwartzman, Torsten V. Zache, Hannes Pichler, and H. R. Sadeghpour

Real-time evolution and sᴡᴀᴘ operations are combined to efficiently suppress excited-state populations using multiple copies of the quantum system.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033033] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a unitary multi-copy protocol that combines real-time evolution and swap operations to simulate imaginary time evolution, enabling efficient suppression of excited-state populations for ground state preparation.
motivation: Preparing ground states of quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum simulation and understanding condensed matter physics, but existing methods are often resource-intensive or rely on non-unitary operations.
method: The proposed method uses multiple copies of the quantum system and interleaves real-time evolution with swap operations to effectively implement imaginary-time evolution, which drives the system to its ground state by exponentially suppressing excited-state components.
result: The protocol efficiently suppresses excited-state populations, as demonstrated in the paper, leading to ground state preparation with a polynomial overhead in copies and evolution time.
conclusion: This approach offers a new unitary, multi-copy strategy for ground state preparation that may be more viable for near-term quantum devices than other known methods.

tldr: This paper introduces a quantum fast multipole method to simulate electronic structure with the lowest known asymptotic complexity in particle number.
motivation: Quantum simulation of electronic structure is vital for chemistry, but existing algorithms have high complexity, limiting practical applications.
method: The authors develop a quantum version of the fast multipole method for efficient Coulomb potential summation within a quantum algorithm framework.
result: They achieve the lowest known asymptotic complexity in particle number for quantum simulation of electronic structure.
conclusion: This work enhances the practicality of quantum simulations for larger molecular systems, potentially impacting quantum chemistry.

title: Faster Algorithmic Quantum And Classical Simulations By Corrected Product Formulas
authors: Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, And Alán Aspuru-Guzik
abstract:

Injecting carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas is shown to significantly improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy with little cost increase, enabling a target accuracy to be reached with substantially lower circuit depth.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033018] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to improve product formulas for Hamiltonian simulation by injecting carefully designed auxiliary terms, achieving higher accuracy with little cost increase and enabling target accuracy with substantially lower circuit depth.
motivation: Product formulas are a common method for Hamiltonian simulation but suffer from limited accuracy; improving them can reduce the computational resources needed for quantum simulations.
method: The authors propose injecting auxiliary terms into product formulas to correct leading-order errors, allowing a smaller error for the same order of formula and thus lower circuit depth.
result: They demonstrate significant improvements in simulation accuracy for a negligible increase in cost, effectively reducing the circuit depth required to reach a given target accuracy.
conclusion: Corrected product formulas offer a more efficient approach to Hamiltonian simulation, beneficial for both quantum and classical simulation algorithms.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang

[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: Introduces systematic cluster corrections to belief propagation for tensor network contraction, yielding polynomial-time algorithms with rigorous error bounds.
motivation: Exact tensor network contraction is #P-hard, and belief propagation approximations lack rigorous accuracy guarantees.
method: They add cluster-based corrections to belief propagation to systematically improve accuracy and derive rigorous bounds on approximation error.
result: The proposed algorithms run in polynomial time and exhibit exponential convergence to the exact contraction value.
conclusion: Offers a new practical method for tensor network contraction with strong theoretical guarantees.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that quantum neural networks intrinsically preserve plasticity during continual learning, unlike classical neural networks.
motivation: Continual learning in classical neural networks suffers from catastrophic forgetting, and quantum counterparts may offer advantages.
method: The authors likely analyze or simulate quantum neural networks under continual learning scenarios to explore plasticity retention.
result: Quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, suggesting long-term learning capabilities.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks may be more suitable for continual learning tasks than classical ones.

tldr: This paper develops an ion mobility spectrometer to measure reduced mobilities of lutetium cations, investigating relativistic effects on electronic structure.
motivation: Relativistic effects significantly influence the electronic structure and properties of heavy elements, and precise characterization requires experimental probes like ion mobility that are sensitive to electronic states.
method: Built a cryogenic ion mobility spectrometer to measure the reduced mobility of Lu+ ions, a parameter that depends on the ion's collision cross-section and hence its electronic configuration.
result: The measurements provide data on Lu+ ion mobility, which can be used to infer information about its electronic state and relativistic contributions to its structure.
conclusion: The technique offers a new experimental approach to study electronic states of heavy ions, aiding the understanding of relativistic effects in atomic physics.

motivation: Understanding the microscopic energy exchange between lattice and spin degrees of freedom is essential for developing next-generation spintronic and magnonic devices.
method: The authors employ transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy to probe nonequilibrium spin dynamics in antiferromagnetic Co3O4 following photoexcitation.

title: Quantum Versus Thermal Fluctuations In Phase Transitions Of Two-dimensional Superconductors

tldr: This paper investigates how quantum and thermal phase fluctuations suppress superconducting order in two-dimensional systems within the quantum XY model.
motivation: Understanding the distinct roles of quantum and thermal fluctuations in suppressing superconductivity is crucial for fundamental physics and potential quantum technologies.
method: The authors perform extensive numerical simulations of the two-dimensional quantum XY model with on-site interaction terms that govern quantum phase fluctuations.
result: The study likely reveals quantitative differences in how quantum and thermal fluctuations affect the phase transition, influencing critical behavior and the superconducting phase.
conclusion: The findings clarify the interplay of quantum and thermal fluctuations in 2D superconductors, providing insights that may guide future theoretical and experimental work.

title: Evolving Ergodic Flows In Confined Geometry
authors: Akshay Seethamraju, R. Aravinda Narayanan, And V. Meenakshi

motivation: To develop a method for quantifying the spatiotemporal evolution of system states in far-from-equilibrium systems, specifically applied to mixing processes in confined geometry.
method: A descriptor based on instantaneous, spatially resolved measurements is used to construct an ergodic measure, which is then applied to analyze the mixing process in confined water-glycerol flows.
result: The approach provides a quantitative characterization of mixing dynamics, demonstrating its utility in far-from-equilibrium systems.
conclusion: The state-based ergodic framework offers a new tool for analyzing mixing and spatiotemporal evolution in complex flows, with potential applications beyond fluid dynamics.

conclusion: The work contributes to understanding and enhancing analog solvers, though it is not aligned with the specified research directions.

authors: Zhou-Quan Wan, Roeland Wiersema, And Shiwei Zhang
abstract:

A Monte Carlo postprocessing method called blurred sampling eliminates infinite variance and systematic bias in variational quantum many-body simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031059] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a blurred sampling postprocessing method that removes infinite variance and systematic bias in variational Monte Carlo for quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Variational Monte Carlo simulations suffer from pathological infinite variance and bias due to nodal and support-mismatch issues, limiting accuracy.
method: The method, called blurred sampling, is a Monte Carlo postprocessing technique that suitably modifies the sampling distribution to mitigate these pathologies.
result: The approach eliminates infinite variance and systematic bias, improving the reliability and accuracy of variational quantum many-body simulations.
conclusion: Blurred sampling offers a practical fix to common VMC pathologies, potentially enhancing the quality of variational calculations in many-body physics.

method: A cold Rydberg gas is used as a dissipative many-body system, and spectral topology is mapped out, likely through spectroscopic measurements.
result: Interaction-driven winding numbers and nonreciprocal behavior dependent on scan direction are observed.
conclusion: The findings demonstrate non-Hermitian topology in cold Rydberg gases, providing a platform for studying dissipative quantum phases.

The SNO+ Collaboration reports new results on reactor antineutrino oscillations using data acquired from May 2022 through July 2025. The spectral analysis of a flux dominated by nuclear reactors at 240, 340, and 350 km yields the mass-squared difference ${m}_{21}^{2}=(7.9{1}_{−0.25}^{+0.22…

result: The extended LEFM model successfully describes crack nucleation below the Griffith length at a critical stress threshold, as well as dynamic fracture behavior.
conclusion: The results suggest that the extended LEFM provides a unified description of various fracture phenomena, including nucleation and dynamic crack growth.

motivation: Understanding the interplay between geometrical frustration and the Kondo effect in strongly correlated electron systems is a key problem in condensed matter physics, and CePdAl provides a model system due to its quasi-kagome structure.
method: High-sensitivity magnetization measurements were performed at temperatures down to 80 mK to observe the magnetic behavior and identify metamagnetic transitions.
result: Clear first-order metamagnetic transitions without magnetization plateaus were observed, indicating a lifting of frustration and a complex competition between the Kondo effect and magnetic ordering.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the nature of the frustrated magnetic ground state and the role of the Kondo effect in this heavy-fermion compound.

method: Analyzed proton-proton collision data at sqrt(s)=13 TeV recorded by the CMS detector, looking for final states with a Higgs boson and two vector bosons, using event categories sensitive to vector-boson scattering.
result: No significant excess over background was observed; upper limits were set on the production cross section, which were interpreted as constraints on the Higgs self-coupling constants.

tldr: This paper experimentally studies the dynamic behavior of metal conductors under intense current pulses, focusing on magnetic compression and solid-liquid phase transitions, measured via Photon Doppler Velocimetry (PDV).
motivation: To better understand the motion, equation-of-state, and electrical conductivity of conductors during solid-liquid phase transitions under extreme current pulses, which are critical for pulsed power physics and engineering.
method: The authors use Photon Doppler Velocimetry (PDV) to measure the velocity of the conductor surface, inferring material properties and phase transition behavior during rapid magnetic compression.
result: The study reports novel measurements of the solid-liquid phase transition dynamics in current-carrying conductors, providing data that can inform models of material behavior under extreme electromagnetic stress.
conclusion: The work contributes to the empirical understanding of material response in pulsed-power systems, but it is entirely unrelated to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033276] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents guidelines for controlling the size of chemically active droplets formed by liquid-liquid phase separation.
motivation: Biological cells and synthetic analogues rely on liquid-liquid phase separation to compartmentalize environments, but controlling the size of coexisting droplets is challenging because large droplets tend to grow at the expense of smaller ones.
method: The authors likely develop theoretical models or simulations to study how chemical activity and reaction kinetics influence droplet size distribution and stability.
result: The paper provides practical guidelines for achieving controlled droplet sizes, potentially relevant for synthetic biology and materials science.
conclusion: The findings offer design rules for controlling droplet sizes in active emulsions, advancing applications in compartmentalization and synthetic cells.

title: Disordered Yet Directed: The Emergence Of Polar Flocks With Disordered Interactions

abstract:

Flocking is a prime example of how robust collective behavior can emerge from simple interaction rules. The flocking transition has been studied extensively since the inception of the original Vicsek model. Here, we introduce a self-propelled particle model with quenched disorder in the pairwise ali…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033279] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: A self-propelled particle model with quenched disorder in pairwise interactions reveals how polar flocks can emerge despite disorder.
motivation: To understand how robust collective behavior like flocking emerges when interaction rules are disordered, extending classic Vicsek-type models.
method: Introduces a self-propelled particle model with quenched disorder in pairwise alignment interactions and analyzes collective order via simulations or theory.
result: Shows that polar order can still emerge even with disordered interactions, with distinctive properties compared to the standard Vicsek transition.
conclusion: Disorder in interactions does not necessarily destroy flocking but can lead to directed collective motion under certain conditions.

title: Climate Network Characterization Of The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation Edge State
authors: Laure Moinat, Reyk Börner, Valerio Lucarini, Maura Brunetti, And Henk A. Dijkstra

tldr: This paper uses climate network analysis to characterize the edge state of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC), a critical tipping element in the Earth system.
motivation: The AMOC is a vital component of the climate system that may collapse under climate change, so robust methods to assess its stability and detect early warning signals are urgently needed.
method: The authors construct climate networks from relevant oceanographic data and analyze network properties such as connectivity and community structure to characterize the AMOC's edge state and its proximity to a tipping point.
result: The study provides a network-based fingerprint of the AMOC's resilience, potentially identifying early warning indicators of its collapse.
conclusion: Climate networks offer a valuable tool for monitoring and understanding tipping elements like the AMOC, improving our ability to anticipate abrupt climate changes.

result: Identified two doping regimes of interest, notably at one-quarter filling.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of electron-phonon physics in triangular lattice systems, potentially relevant to charge density waves or superconductivity.

authors: M. Menéndez, Lan Hoang Mai, Nazifa Tasnim Arony, Henry Carfagno, Lauren N. Mccabe, Joshua M. O. Zide, Cefe López, Matthew F. Doty, And P. D. García

Disorder in photonic lattices creates localized states inside the photonic band gap. The energy distribution of these states is often described as a Lifshitz tail, even though it is inconsistent with Lifshitz statistics near the band edge. Here, we show that in photonic-crystal waveguides with inten…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033271] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates disorder-induced localized states in photonic-crystal waveguides and reveals the anisotropic nature of the Urbach tail, correcting the common Lifshitz tail description.
motivation: Disorder in photonic lattices creates localized states inside the photonic band gap, and accurately modeling their energy distribution is crucial for understanding photonic transport and localization phenomena.
method: The authors study photonic-crystal waveguides with intentional disorder, contrasting the observed energy distribution with predictions from Lifshitz statistics and analyzing the anisotropic behavior of the Urbach tail.
result: They demonstrate that the energy distribution of localized states deviates from Lifshitz statistics near the band edge and exhibits anisotropy in different propagation directions.
conclusion: The work corrects existing models of photonic band-tail states, providing a more accurate understanding of disorder effects in photonic structures, though it has no direct connection to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

motivation: To probe beyond Standard Model physics, specifically the QCD axion's coupling to quarks, using rare kaon decay data.
method: A fully reproducible likelihood analysis of NA62 K+→π+νν̄ data, including a complete renormalization-group evolution of the relevant operators.
result: The analysis provides constraints on the vectorial axion-down-strange coupling, improving over previous limits.
conclusion: The results contribute to axion searches but are unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

method: Theoretical analysis of strong-field laser-plasma interactions to induce and study two-photon synchrotron emission.
result: Demonstrates that laser-plasma systems can effectively enable investigations of nonlinear QED phenomena.
conclusion: This approach provides a promising new avenue for experimental and theoretical exploration of relativistic nonlinear QED effects.

result: The findings reveal distinct behaviors in the two stages, providing insights into how supercooling affects crystallization kinetics.

result: They find unambiguous evidence of cluster crystals formed by the binary mixture, where multiple particles occupy a lattice site.
conclusion: This study demonstrates the existence of binary cluster crystals, expanding the known range of crystalline phases for ultrasoft particles.

authors: I. Shitrit, O. Lauber Bonomo, And S. Reuveni
abstract:
Author(s): I. Shitrit, O. Lauber Bonomo, and S. Reuveni

While pushing is intuitively associated with progress, it can surprisingly cause tracers moving in disordered environments to become permanently confined. This study shows that confinement is a result of irreversible “door-closing” events, providing a minimal description of pushing-induced arrest across lattices and dimensions.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032036] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how pushing in disordered environments can lead to permanent confinement of tracers, due to irreversible door-closing events.
motivation: To understand the counterintuitive effect where pushing, which usually aids progress, can cause arrest in disordered systems.
method: The study provides a minimal description of pushing-induced arrest across lattices and dimensions, likely using analytical or simulation approaches.
result: Confinement is shown to result from irreversible door-closing events.
conclusion: The work establishes a minimal framework for understanding pushing-induced arrest in disordered environments.

result: They successfully transported one or two particles along arbitrary prescribed trajectories using this technique.
conclusion: Water-wave interference provides a versatile and dynamic method for particle manipulation, which could have applications in microscale transport and sorting.

motivation: Spontaneous degradation of thermoelectric materials affects long-term performance; understanding whether intrinsic defect relaxations or external stimuli cause this is crucial for materials stability and design.

conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of intrinsic defects in material aging and suggest that controlling defect relaxation could improve thermoelectric material stability.

conclusion: This provides new insight into the electronic properties of nickelates, potentially relevant for understanding superconductivity.
