authors: Shuai Zhang, Yanyu Jia, Atanu Samanta, Yutian Bao, Haosen Guan, Zhaoyi Joy Zheng, Guangming Cheng, Ting Liu, Cangyu Qu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Nan Yao, Ashlie Martini, Leslie Schoop, Andrew M. Rappe, Sanfeng Wu, And Robert W. Carpick
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Zhang, Yanyu Jia, Atanu Samanta, Yutian Bao, Haosen Guan, Zhaoyi Joy Zheng, Guangming Cheng, Ting Liu, Cangyu Qu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Nan Yao, Ashlie Martini, Leslie Schoop, Andrew M. Rappe, Sanfeng Wu, and Robert W. Carpick

A large stress generated by a small tip drives a reaction between two materials in an 2D encapsulated space to produce a new material with interesting electronic properties that can be written into patterns as small as 50 nm.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031029] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: A mechanochemical nano-writing technique uses a tip-induced stress to create atomically thin metal patterns as small as 50 nm.
motivation: To develop a simple method for creating structured atomic-thin materials with tailored electronic properties.
method: A tip applies large stress to drive a reaction between two materials in a confined 2D space, producing a metal layer that can be patterned.
result: The technique enables writing metal patterns with nanoscale resolution (down to 50 nm) and the produced material exhibits useful electronic properties.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a new approach to nano-manufacturing of 2D materials with potential applications in nano-electronics.

title: Editorial: Closing Special Collection On 2d Materials

method: Publication of an editorial in Physical Review X.
result: Announcement of the collection's closure.

title: High-Dimensional Dynamics In Low-Dimensional Networks
authors: Yue Wan And Robert Rosenbaum
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Wan and Robert Rosenbaum

The relationship between the dimensionality of a network’s structure and its dynamics is investigated, showing that networks with low-dimensional structures can produce either high- or low-dimensional responses.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031025] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper explores how low-dimensional network structures can lead to either high- or low-dimensional responses, highlighting the complex relationship between network architecture and dynamics.
motivation: To understand the relationship between the dimensionality of a network's structure and the dimensionality of its dynamics, which is fundamental for modeling complex systems.
method: The authors presumably analyze theoretical or computational models of networks with controlled structural dimensionality and measure the resulting dynamical responses.
result: It is shown that low-dimensional structures do not necessarily constrain dynamics to low dimensions; both high- and low-dimensional responses can emerge.
conclusion: The findings suggest that structural dimensionality alone does not determine dynamical complexity, with implications for the design and interpretation of network models.

title: Predicting Liquid Properties And Behavior Via Droplet Pinch-off And Machine Learning
authors: Jingtao Wang, Qiwei Chen, C. Ricardo Constante-Amores, Denise Gorse, Alfonso Arturo Castrejón-Pita, And José Rafael Castrejón-Pita
abstract:
Author(s): Jingtao Wang, Qiwei Chen, C. Ricardo Constante-Amores, Denise Gorse, Alfonso Arturo Castrejón-Pita, and José Rafael Castrejón-Pita

A powerful method allows hard to measure properties like viscosity and surface tension to be determined from a single, high-speed snapshot.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031021] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning on droplet pinch-off snapshots to predict liquid properties such as viscosity and surface tension.
motivation: To provide a powerful and simple method for determining hard-to-measure liquid properties from a single high-speed image.
method: High-speed imaging captures droplet pinch-off dynamics, and machine learning models are trained to correlate features of the pinch-off process with the target liquid properties.
result: The method successfully predicts viscosity and surface tension from the snapshots, demonstrating accuracy in characterizing liquids.
conclusion: Droplet pinch-off combined with machine learning offers a novel and efficient approach for liquid property measurement.

title: Statistical Physics Of Deep Learning: Optimal Learning Of A Multilayer Perceptron Near Interpolation
authors: Jean Barbier, Francesco Camilli, Minh-Toan Nguyen, Mauro Pastore, And Rudy Skerk
abstract:
Author(s): Jean Barbier, Francesco Camilli, Minh-Toan Nguyen, Mauro Pastore, and Rudy Skerk

Using statistical physics and random matrix theory, researchers derive the generalization error of a deep fully connected neural network and uncover the mechanisms governing its behavior as feature learning progressively propagates across layers.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031014] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Uses statistical physics and random matrix theory to derive generalization error of deep fully connected neural networks near interpolation.
motivation: To understand the behavior of deep learning models in the interpolation regime using tools from statistical physics.
method: Applies statistical physics and random matrix theory to analyze a multilayer perceptron.
result: Derives the generalization error and reveals mechanisms of feature learning propagation across layers.
conclusion: Provides theoretical insights into deep learning from a statistical physics perspective.

title: Identifying Geometric Third-Order Nonlinear Transport In Disordered Materials
authors: Zhen-Hao Gong, Zhi-Hao Wei, Hai-Zhou Lu, And X. C. Xie
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen-Hao Gong, Zhi-Hao Wei, Hai-Zhou Lu, and X. C. Xie

A theoretical data-analysis tool resolves the chaotic interpretation of nonlinear electronic transport data, providing a structured method to extract quantum geometric properties from realistic materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031012] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: A data-analysis tool extracts quantum geometric properties from nonlinear transport in disordered materials.
motivation: To resolve chaotic interpretations of nonlinear electronic transport data and provide a structured method for extracting quantum geometric properties.
method: Theoretical data-analysis framework applied to transport data.
result: Demonstrates a method to extract quantum geometric properties from realistic materials.
conclusion: The tool is useful for interpreting nonlinear transport data in disordered systems.

title: Waves Maintain Large-Scale 2d Flows In Rotating Turbulence And Cause Their Demise
authors: Sébastien Gomé And Anna Frishman
abstract:
Author(s): Sébastien Gomé and Anna Frishman

A first-principles approach helps explain energy transfer from 3D wave excitation to 2D structures in rotating turbulent flow.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031013] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a first-principles explanation of how waves transfer energy from 3D wave excitation to 2D structures in rotating turbulent flows.
motivation: Understanding the mechanisms behind large-scale 2D flow formation and decay in rotating turbulence is important for atmospheric and oceanic dynamics.
method: The authors develop a first-principles theoretical approach to analyze energy transfer between 3D waves and 2D flows.
result: They find that waves can both maintain large-scale 2D flows and trigger their demise, depending on the energy transfer dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a deeper insight into the role of waves in rotating turbulence, with implications for predicting large-scale flow behavior.

title: Machine Learning-driven Hubbard $u$ Prediction For High-throughput Study Of High-pressure Manganese Oxides
authors: Bingqing Cao, Wenming Xia, Jing Zhao, And Xianlong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingqing Cao, Wenming Xia, Jing Zhao, and Xianlong Wang

As prototypical strongly correlated materials, manganese oxides serve as key platforms for studying electronic correlations. Under high pressure, drastic changes in local coordination, bond lengths, and electronic screening modify the electron correlation strength. However, due to the difficulty in …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134102] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies machine learning to predict Hubbard U parameters for high-throughput studies of manganese oxides under high pressure.
motivation: Understanding electronic correlations in manganese oxides under high pressure requires accurate Hubbard U values, which are typically expensive to compute via first-principles methods. A fast and accurate prediction method is needed for high-throughput screening.
method: The authors develop a machine learning model to predict Hubbard U values, likely trained on a dataset of existing DFT+U calculations, and apply it to high-pressure manganese oxides.
result: The model enables efficient and accurate prediction of U parameters, facilitating high-throughput computational studies of correlated materials under extreme conditions.
conclusion: Machine learning-based prediction of Hubbard U is a promising approach to accelerate first-principles studies of strongly correlated materials under variable pressure.

title: Identification Of $^{17}\mathrm{Na}$ Ground State And Mirror Symmetry Violation With $^{17}\mathrm{C}$
authors: L. Ni et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): L. Ni et al.

The ground state of the three-proton emitter [MATH] has been identified. Energy correlations between the protons and the [MATH] residue indicate that its decay is sequential initiated by the emission of a single proton to the ground state of [MATH] followed by simu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 102501] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies the ground state of 17Na and discusses mirror symmetry violation with 17C based on energy correlations from its three-proton decay.
motivation: To identify the ground state of the three-proton emitter 17Na and to investigate mirror symmetry violation between 17Na and 17C, which is of interest in nuclear structure physics.
method: Energy correlations between the emitted protons and the 13C residue were measured to determine the decay mechanism and infer the ground state properties of 17Na.
result: The decay was found to be sequential, initiated by single-proton emission to the ground state of 13N, and the ground state of 17Na has been identified.
conclusion: The study provides experimental evidence for mirror symmetry violation in the 17Na-17C pair, contributing to understanding nuclear forces under asymmetric conditions.

title: Dissipative Continuation For Ground-state Preparation At Chemical Transition States
authors: Thomas W. Watts, Soumya Sarkar, Daniel Collins, Nam Nguyen, Luke Quezada, Michael J. Bremner, And Samuel J. Elman
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas W. Watts, Soumya Sarkar, Daniel Collins, Nam Nguyen, Luke Quezada, Michael J. Bremner, and Samuel J. Elman

Simulating chemical reactions exhibits a pronounced unevenness in computational difficulty: While equilibrium reactant and product geometries are often tractable, transition-state (TS) geometries frequently display strong multireference character that challenges both classical solvers and coherent q…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022471] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a dissipative continuation method for preparing ground states of chemical transition states on quantum computers, addressing strong multireference character.
motivation: Chemical transition states exhibit strong multireference character that is computationally challenging for both classical and quantum solvers, motivating a need for efficient ground-state preparation methods.
method: The authors introduce a dissipative continuation approach that likely guides the system from an easy-to-prepare state to the target transition state by controlling dissipation and continuity of the Hamiltonian.
result: The paper reports that the dissipative continuation technique enables ground-state preparation at chemical transition states, overcoming previous limitations for systems with strong multireference character.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a practical route for simulating chemical reactions at transition states on quantum devices, relevant to quantum chemistry applications.

title: Staggering Dominolike Blast Front Motion In A One-dimensional Cold Gas
authors: Taras Holovatch, Yuri Kozitsky, Krzysztof Pilorz, And Yurij Holovatch

[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034105] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: A study of blast front propagation in a one-dimensional alternating-mass particle system, revealing a staggered, domino-like motion.
motivation: To understand the connection between microscopic Newtonian dynamics and macroscopic hydrodynamic blast wave behavior using alternating particle systems.
method: Analyzing a one-dimensional model of point particles with alternating masses and deriving the motion of the blast front.
result: The blast front exhibits staggered, domino-like propagation characteristics.
conclusion: The model provides insights into how corpuscular dynamics give rise to hydrodynamic phenomena.

title: Entropy Of Full Covering Of The Kagome Lattice By Straight Trimers
authors: Deepak Dhar, Tiago J. Oliveira, R. Rajesh, And Jürgen F. Stilck
abstract:
Author(s): Deepak Dhar, Tiago J. Oliveira, R. Rajesh, and Jürgen F. Stilck

We consider the number of ways all the sites of a kagome lattice can be covered by nonoverlapping linear rigid rods where each rod covers three sites. We establish a two-to-one correspondence between the configurations of trimers on the kagome lattice to the covering by dimers of a related hexagonal…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024156] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper computes the entropy of full coverings of the kagome lattice by straight trimers, establishing a correspondence with dimer coverings on a related hexagonal lattice.
motivation: To determine the number of ways rigid trimers can cover the kagome lattice, which is a classic combinatorial problem in statistical mechanics.
method: The authors establish a two-to-one mapping between trimer configurations on the kagome lattice and dimer coverings of an associated hexagonal lattice, then use known techniques for enumerating dimer coverings.
result: They derive an exact expression for the entropy per site of the trimer covering.
conclusion: The work provides a closed-form result for this lattice statistics problem, contributing to the understanding of hard-core lattice models.

title: Accelerated Deep Atomic Potential Transformer For Long-range Machine Learning Force Fields Without Graphs
authors: Evan Dramko, Yizhi Zhu, Yihuang Xiong, Geoffroy Hautier, Thomas Reps, Christopher Jermaine, And Anastasios Kyrillidis
abstract:
Author(s): Evan Dramko, Yizhi Zhu, Yihuang Xiong, Geoffroy Hautier, Thomas Reps, Christopher Jermaine, and Anastasios Kyrillidis

Point defects play a central role in driving the properties of materials. First-principles methods are widely used to compute defect energetics and structures, including at scale for high-throughput defect databases. However, these methods are computationally expensive, making machine learning force…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033266] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a transformer-based machine learning force field that efficiently captures long-range atomic interactions without graph construction, targeting defect energetics in materials.
motivation: First-principles methods for defect energetics are computationally prohibitive, especially for high-throughput studies, motivating the need for faster and accurate machine learning surrogates.
method: The authors design a deep atomic potential transformer that processes atomic structures without explicit graph representations, enabling long-range interaction modeling while accelerating computation.
result: The model reportedly achieves accurate defect energetics with significant speedups, enabling large-scale defect simulations.
conclusion: This work advances computational materials science but is unrelated to the specified research directions in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Search For New Physics Via Low-Energy Electron Recoils With A 4.2 Tonne-Year Exposure From The Lz Experiment
authors: D. S. Akerib et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): D. S. Akerib et al. (The LZ Collaboration)

We report results from searches for new physics models through electron recoils using data collected by the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment during its first two science runs, with a total exposure of [MATH]. The observed data are consistent with a background-…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 101803] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports results from the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment searching for new physics via low-energy electron recoils, with data consistent with background.
motivation: To search for new physics models, such as dark matter or exotic particles, through electron recoil interactions in a large liquid xenon detector.
method: The LZ experiment collected data over two science runs totaling a 4.2 tonne-year exposure and analyzed low-energy electron recoil events for signals beyond the standard model.
result: Observed data are consistent with background expectations, setting new limits on various new physics models.
conclusion: The null result constrains possible new physics models that could produce low-energy electron recoils.

title: Infrared Singularities Of Multileg Amplitudes With A Massive Particle At Three Loops
authors: Einan Gardi And Zehao Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Einan Gardi and Zehao Zhu

We determine the complete three-loop QCD soft anomalous dimension for multileg amplitudes involving a single massive colored particle and any number of massless ones. This is achieved by applying a novel strategy based on a light-cone expansion of correlators of semi-infinite Wilson lines using the …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 101901] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes the complete three-loop QCD soft anomalous dimension for amplitudes with a single massive colored particle and any number of massless particles, using a light-cone expansion of Wilson line correlators.
motivation: To advance the understanding of infrared singularities in multi-leg scattering amplitudes involving massive particles, which is crucial for precision phenomenology in high-energy physics.
method: The authors employ a novel light-cone expansion technique for semi-infinite Wilson line correlators to systematically determine the soft anomalous dimension at three loops in QCD.
result: They obtain the complete three-loop QCD soft anomalous dimension for the specified amplitude class, extending previous results and verifying consistency with known structure.
conclusion: This work provides a key theoretical ingredient for resummation and precise predictions in processes involving massive colored particles, though it is outside the scope of quantum information or related fields.

title: Nmr Evidence Of Pairing Fluctuations Above ${T}_{c}$ And Absence Of Spin Magnetism In The Time-reversal Symmetry-breaking State Of ${\mathrm{Ba}}_{1−x}{\mathrm{K}}_{x}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Florian Bärtl, Nadia Stegani, Federico Caglieris, Ilya Shipulin, Yongwei Li, Ruidan Zhong, Quanxin Hu, Yu Zheng, Chi-Ming Yim, Sven Luther, Jochen Wosnitza, Rajib Sarkar, Hans-Henning Klauss, Julien Garaud, Albert Samoilenka, Anton Talkachov, Egor Babaev, Hannes Kühne, And Vadim Grinenko
abstract:
Author(s): Florian Bärtl, Nadia Stegani, Federico Caglieris, Ilya Shipulin, Yongwei Li, Ruidan Zhong, Quanxin Hu, Yu Zheng, Chi-Ming Yim, Sven Luther, Jochen Wosnitza, Rajib Sarkar, Hans-Henning Klauss, Julien Garaud, Albert Samoilenka, Anton Talkachov, Egor Babaev, Hannes Kühne, and Vadim Grinenko

Four- or higher-order fermionic condensates can form in non-BCS multicomponent superconductors. Here, the authors present spectroscopic evidence for pairing correlations that appear well above the superconducting critical temperature in the highly overdoped Ba−xK
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134504] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: NMR and muSR measurements on an iron-based superconductor reveal pairing correlations above Tc and a homogeneous time-reversal symmetry breaking state without spin magnetism.
motivation: To understand the nature of unconventional superconductivity and the origin of broken time-reversal symmetry in iron-based superconductors.
method: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and muon spin rotation (muSR) experiments on highly overdoped Ba1-xKxFe2As2 were performed to detect pairing fluctuations above the critical temperature and to probe magnetic order.
result: Spectroscopic evidence shows pairing correlations well above Tc and indicates that the time-reversal symmetry breaking state is homogeneous and not associated with conventional spin magnetism.
conclusion: The broken time-reversal symmetry in this superconductor is likely due to multicomponent superconducting order, not magnetic ordering.

title: Computational Prediction Of Strontium Carbide Phases Under Compression
authors: Nikita Rybin, Evgeny Moerman, Pranab Gain, Artem R. Oganov, And Alexander Shapeev
abstract:
Author(s): Nikita Rybin, Evgeny Moerman, Pranab Gain, Artem R. Oganov, and Alexander Shapeev

Exploring the chemistry of materials at high pressures enables the discovery of previously unknown, but frequently exotic, compounds. We systematically searched for all thermodynamically stable Sr-C compounds under pressure (up to 100 GPa) using the ab initio evolutionary crystal structure predictio…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154102] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper computationally predicts stable strontium carbide phases under high pressure using evolutionary crystal structure prediction.
motivation: To discover new exotic compounds at high pressures, specifically studying Sr-C compounds up to 100 GPa.
method: Used ab initio evolutionary crystal structure prediction to systematically search for thermodynamically stable Sr-C compounds.
result: Identified several stable phases of strontium carbide at various pressures.
conclusion: The study expands the known chemistry of strontium-carbide under extreme conditions.

title: Competing Ru Magnetic Orders In The Spin-1 $xy$ Pyrochlore ${\mathrm{Nd}}_{2}{\mathrm{Ru}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$
authors: Poonam Yadav, Jae Hyuck Lee, Heung-Sik Kim, Dongjoon Song, A. Dominic Fortes, Changyoung Kim, And Sungkyun Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Poonam Yadav, Jae Hyuck Lee, Heung-Sik Kim, Dongjoon Song, A. Dominic Fortes, Changyoung Kim, and Sungkyun Choi

Magnetic pyrochlore oxides exhibit various unconventional electronic phases and excitations due to geometric frustration. Recently, a collective magnetic excitation was reported in Raman spectroscopy on a pyrochlore ruthenate [MATH]. However, its origin …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154405] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates competing magnetic orders and the origin of collective magnetic excitations in the spin-1 xy pyrochlore Nd2Ru2O7.
motivation: To understand the unusual magnetic excitations observed in pyrochlore ruthenates, which arise from geometric frustration.
method: Combines experimental characterization (likely neutron diffraction and Raman spectroscopy) with theoretical modeling to identify the magnetic ground state.
result: Identifies competing Ru magnetic orders and explains the observed collective excitation in terms of these orders.
conclusion: Provides insight into the magnetic properties of Nd2Ru2O7, relevant to frustrated magnetism but unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Intruder Dynamics In Granular Media Under Localized Surface Loading
authors: E. M. Franklin, B. Darbois Texier, A. Seguin, D. D. Carvalho, And Y. Bertho
abstract:
Author(s): E. M. Franklin, B. Darbois Texier, A. Seguin, D. D. Carvalho, and Y. Bertho

We experimentally investigate the dynamics of a spherical intruder driven horizontally at a constant force in a granular medium subjected to a localized surface overload. While intruder motion beneath a free surface exhibits constant acceleration in the quasistatic regime, the presence of a surface …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035408] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental observations of intruder motion in granular media under localized surface loading, showing how surface overload modifies the quasistatic acceleration behavior.
motivation: To understand how localized surface loading affects the dynamics of an intruder moving through granular material, which is relevant for geophysics and industrial processes.
method: Experiments were performed with a spherical intruder driven horizontally at constant force in a granular medium, with a localized surface overload applied, and the motion was tracked.
result: The presence of a surface overload changes the intruder's motion from constant acceleration to a different regime, indicating the influence of stress distribution.
conclusion: Localized surface loading significantly alters intruder dynamics in granular media, which has implications for understanding penetration and drag in such systems.

title: Turning Without Fins: Quantifying The Distinct Kinematics And Vortex Dynamics Of Maneuvering Swimming Snakes
authors: Elizabeth Gregorio, Ramiro Godoy-Diana, And Anthony Herrel
abstract:
Author(s): Elizabeth Gregorio, Ramiro Godoy-Diana, and Anthony Herrel

The agile turning maneuvers of anguilliform swimmers remain one of the least studied aspects of aquatic locomotion, despite being crucial for survival in underwater environments. To change direction, animals must find a balance between minimizing their moment of inertia and maximizing torque. Anguil…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024410] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the kinematics and vortex dynamics of turning maneuvers in anguilliform swimming snakes.
motivation: To understand the agile turning abilities of anguilliform swimmers, which are crucial for survival but poorly understood.
method: The study quantifies the distinct kinematics and vortex dynamics during maneuvering turns, likely through experimental observation and fluid dynamics analysis.
result: The paper provides detailed insights into how snakes balance moment of inertia and torque during turns.
conclusion: Enhances understanding of aquatic locomotion and turning performance in limbless swimmers.

title: Magnetic Compression And A Kinematic Signature Of Surface Melting In Current-driven Metal Loads
authors: A. W. Klemmer, S. E. Kreher, T. M. Hutchinson, E. P. Yu, T. J. Awe, C. L. Rousculp, D. H. Dolan, B. T. Hutsel, K. C. Yates, K. J. Swanson, J. J. Iratcabal, A. Dahal, And B. S. Bauer

In current-driven metal loads, a nonlinear magnetic-diffusion wave carries current and Joule heating inward from the electrical skin-depth layer, coupling the electromagnetic drive to material compression, melting, and expansion. Photon Doppler velocimetry of electrically thick aluminum measures pre…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L023202] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates magnetic compression and surface melting in current-driven metal loads using photon Doppler velocimetry, focusing on nonlinear magnetic diffusion and Joule heating.
motivation: To understand how electromagnetic drive couples to material compression and melting in high-current pulsed-power systems.
method: Experimental study employing photon Doppler velocimetry on electrically thick aluminum samples to track surface motion and infer melting during magnetic compression.
result: Identifies a kinematic signature of surface melting from velocimetry data, revealing dynamics of melting under rapid Joule heating and compression.
conclusion: Provides new insights into material behavior under extreme magnetic fields and currents, relevant to pulsed-power and inertial confinement applications.

title: Unraveling Network Dynamics Via Riemannian Filtering Of Network Interactions
authors: Yonatan Kleerekoper, Kesem Shapira, Yonatan Keselman, Sandra Nestler, Mohammad Kurtam, Shai Abramson, Dori Derdikman, Yitzhak Schiller, Simon Musall, And Hadas Benisty

Functional connectivity (FC) is fundamentally nonstationary, undergoing continuous reconfigurations that track shifting behavioral and cognitive states. [Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033277] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a Riemannian filtering approach to analyze nonstationary functional connectivity in brain networks, but it is unrelated to quantum information or physics.
motivation: Functional connectivity is nonstationary and existing methods fail to capture high-dimensional reconfigurations across behavioral states.
method: The authors propose using Riemannian geometry to filter network interactions and track dynamic changes in functional connectivity over time.
result: The method is demonstrated on neural data (likely from experiments), showing improved tracking of network state transitions.
conclusion: Riemannian filtering offers a novel way to unravel network dynamics, but the work is purely in neuroscience and data analysis.

title: Type-I And type-II Saddle Points And A Quasiflat Band In A Bi-pyrochlore Superconductor ${\mathrm{CsBi}}_{2}$
authors: Yusei Morita, Yongkai Li, Yu-Hao Wei, Kosuke Nakayama, Zhiwei Wang, Hua-Yu Li, Takemi Kato, Seigo Souma, Kiyohisa Tanaka, Kenichi Ozawa, Jia-Xin Yin, Takashi Takahashi, Min-Quan Kuang, Yugui Yao, And Takafumi Sato
abstract:

The divergence of the electron density of states (DOS) plays an important role in enhancing many-body interactions and inducing various quantum phases in low-dimensional systems. However, such unique electronic structures remain experimentally elusive in three-dimensional (3D) systems, particularly …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033253] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of type-I and type-II saddle points and a quasiflat band in the 3D superconductor CsBi2, which may enhance many-body interactions.
motivation: The divergence of electron density of states (DOS) can enhance many-body interactions and induce quantum phases, but such features have been elusive in 3D systems.
method: The authors performed experimental electronic structure measurements, likely using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), to investigate the band structure of CsBi2.
result: They identified type-I and type-II saddle points and a quasiflat band, indicating a DOS divergence in a 3D superconductor.
conclusion: The presence of these electronic features may lead to enhanced many-body interactions and potentially novel quantum phases in this material.

title: Production And Decay Dynamics Of The Charmed Baryon ${\mathrm{Λ}}_{c}^{+}$ In ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Annihilations Near Threshold
authors: M. Ablikim et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ablikim et al. (BESIII Collaboration)

Researchers observe the transverse polarization of the charmed baryon Λc+ in electron-positron annihilations using the BESIII detector.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031058] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports the first observation of transverse polarization of the charmed baryon Λ_c^+ in e+e- annihilations near threshold using the BESIII detector.
motivation: To study the production and decay dynamics of charmed baryons, which can reveal insights into the strong interaction and test theoretical models.
method: The BESIII experiment collected data at center-of-mass energies near the Λ_c^+Λ̅_c^- threshold and measured the angular distribution of decay products to extract polarization.
result: They observed a nonzero transverse polarization of the Λ_c^+, contradicting some theoretical expectations.
conclusion: This measurement provides new constraints on the production mechanisms and decay dynamics of charmed baryons.

motivation: To understand the microscopic mechanism of ionic transport in superionic conductors, which are important for energy applications.
method: The authors used neutron scattering techniques (probably inelastic) and possibly simulations to probe phonon dynamics and identify collective atomic hopping.

conclusion: The findings advance the fundamental understanding of superionic transport and may guide future materials design.

Thermal degradation in MgAgSb thermoelectric material can be reversed with low-temperature annealing.

tldr: This paper investigates phase evolution in Mg-Ag-Sb thermoelectric materials and demonstrates that thermal degradation can be reversed via low-temperature annealing.
motivation: To understand and overcome thermal degradation in thermoelectric materials for improved performance and recovery.
method: The study likely combines experimental characterization and computational modeling to analyze phase transitions and microstructural changes.

conclusion: This provides a strategy for designing thermally recoverable thermoelectrics.

title: Riemannian Geometric Classification And Emergent Phenomena Of Magnetic Textures
authors: Koki Shinada And Naoto Nagaosa
abstract:
Author(s): Koki Shinada and Naoto Nagaosa

A classification framework based on differential geometry introduces geodesic and torsional scalar spin chiralities, revealing a quantum geometric effect that modifies electron equations of motion in complex magnetic textures.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031026] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a differential-geometry-based classification of magnetic textures using geodesic and torsional scalar spin chiralities, revealing a quantum geometric effect that modifies electron equations of motion.
motivation: To systematize the classification of complex magnetic textures and understand emergent phenomena arising from their geometry.
method: It introduces a Riemannian geometric framework with novel spin chirality measures and analyzes their impact on electron dynamics.
result: The framework uncovers a quantum geometric correction to electron equations of motion in textured magnets.
conclusion: This work offers a new geometric perspective for understanding emergent phenomena in magnetic systems.

tldr: This paper reports ARPES measurements revealing a three-dimensional electronic structure and strong-coupling pairing regime in superconducting bilayer nickelate films.
motivation: To understand the intrinsic electronic structure and pairing mechanism of nickelate superconductors, which are a novel class of unconventional superconductors.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was performed on high-quality bilayer nickelate thin films to map their band structure.
result: The measurements show a three-dimensional electronic structure and evidence for strong-coupling superconductivity on the orbital band.
conclusion: The findings provide important insight into the electronic properties of nickelate superconductors and help clarify the pairing mechanism in this material family.
